docs.title: Interview Guide — Legal Guardians and Healthcare POA Holders
docs.text:
Notion story: CC-4 Interview guide: legal guardians · CC-197 concept tests of the built features Status: DRAFT v2, updated 2026-11-15 (CC-197). Not yet piloted or used. No interviews have taken place.

Participants come through the CC-1 screener. Do not ask to see legal documents. Do not ask for the elder's name or diagnoses. Session up to 70 minutes (if time is short, drop T5 and T4); many guardians work full time, so offer evenings and weekends.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
1. Understand how the guardian knows, day to day, whether the elder is OK.
  2. Measure the workload: calls, texts, apps, time off work, coordination with caregivers and family.
  3. Understand how they verify that care actually happened (doses, visits) and how much they trust what they hear.
  4. Understand decision-making: what they approve, how they involve the elder, and where they feel the tension between protecting and respecting autonomy.
  5. Learn what proving legal authority has been like (with hospitals, pharmacies, agencies).
  6. React to prototype tasks: today at a glance, approvals, SOS response, and the weekly digest.
  7. React to the everyday features built since October: the evening recap, refill alerts, Maggie's daily check-ins and the family chat.

docs.title: Interviewer reminders
docs.text:
• Guardians often carry guilt and stress. Be warm; allow pauses. Do not offer advice.
  • Ask about the last week, specific events.
  • If they mention a crisis that is ongoing, check they're OK to continue.
  • Run the concept tests on the research phone, never the participant's. After the session, tap Reset demo in the presenter sheet so nothing carries over to the next person.
  • Chat voice: before the session, block the microphone for the prototype site in the research phone's browser (screener §9), so the chat opens its typing box instead of listening. In Chrome and most browsers the chat's voice reply sends speech to an online service, though the screen says it stays on the device (CC-222), and one tap starts it listening to the whole room. Ask what they expect happens to their words if they spoke. Remove this line once CC-222 is done.
  • The demo's medicine names (Metformin, Lisinopril, Vitamin D3, Atorvastatin) belong to the made-up Maggie and are fine in prompts. Never note them as the participant's.

docs.title: 1. Warm-up (5 min)
docs.text:
• Tell me a bit about yourself and the person you care for (relationship, no names).
  • How did you become their POA / guardian?
  • Who else is involved in their care?

docs.title: 2. Knowing they're OK (10 min)
docs.text:
• How did you know yesterday that they were OK? Walk me through it.
  • How many times in a typical day do you call, text or check something?
  • Tell me about the last time you didn't know and worried. What did you do?
  • What are you most afraid of missing?

docs.title: 3. Workload (8 min) — core
docs.text:
• What tools do you use to coordinate? (group texts, calendar, notebook, agency portal, spreadsheet)
  • How much time per week goes to coordinating care? Any time off work?
  • Who do you have to chase for information?
  • What falls through the cracks?

docs.title: 4. Verification and trust (8 min) — core
docs.text:
• How do you know a medicine was actually taken? A visit actually happened?
  • Has there been a time you found out something hadn't been done? How did you find out, and how long later?
  • What proof would be enough without making the caregiver feel watched?
  • How do you want to hear about a missed dose — immediately, after a delay, only if the caregiver doesn't fix it?

docs.title: 5. Decisions and autonomy (10 min) — core
docs.text:
• What kinds of decisions do you make for them? Which do they still make?
  • Tell me about a recent decision. How did you involve them?
  • Has there been a disagreement between what you thought was safe and what they wanted? What happened?
  • If they wanted to stop sharing information with family or the aide for a while, how would you feel? Should that apply to you?
  • Should they be told about every decision you make? Why or why not?

docs.title: 6. Proving authority (4 min)
docs.text:
• When have you had to show your POA or guardianship papers? How did that go?
  • How long would you accept waiting for an app to verify your documents before you get guardian access?

docs.title: 7. Concept test — prototype tasks (12 min)
docs.text:
Use /#/app → Sarah. Use presenter controls to set up scenarios before each task (e.g., Simulate a missed dose).

Task Prompt Watch for Success = T1 Today at a glance "It's 11am. Is Mom OK today?" Time to answer; which signals they trust Answers correctly in under 30 seconds T2 Missed dose (After Simulate a missed dose) "Something needs your attention." Finds the flag; understands escalation order (caregiver first) Identifies the issue and a next action T3 Approval "Ana has asked for a change. Decide." Reads detail; wants to ask Mom first?; notices the elder is notified Approves or declines with a note T4 SOS response (After Maggie presses SOS) "Respond." Finds "I'm on my way"; expectations about calling 911 Acknowledges SOS T5 Weekly digest "Your brother wants a summary of the week." Would they forward it? Is anything missing or too much? Explains what's in it

After each: "1–5, how easy?" and "Would this replace something you do today? What?"

docs.title: 7b. Concept test — everyday care built since October (10 min)
docs.text:
Same phone, still as Sarah. Use the presenter controls named in each task.

Task Prompt Watch for Success = T6 Evening recap (After Skip to 7 PM for the evening recap; the card already shows after 6 PM) "It's evening. How did Mom's day go?" Reads the headline first? With the demo data it isn't a calm day: expect a look at a dose or One refill to sort out. Does the headline match what they then find? Finds See the week; reaction to the 7 PM update and the switch to turn it off Sums up the day correctly in own words T7 Running low (After Simulate low Metformin supply) "Something about Mom's medicines needs sorting." Finds it under Needs your attention (Atorvastatin is already low in the demo, so two medicines show); taps Request refill; the app then says asked Fog City Pharmacy for a refill: do they read that as the app having told the pharmacy? (It only records that Sarah asked.) Notices the Calendar refill entry Requests a refill for either medicine and says roughly when it runs out T8 How she's been feeling "How has Mom been feeling this week?" Then, after Simulate 2 days with no meals logged: "What do you make of this?" Finds Daily check-ins · 7 days under Health; reaction to Mom deciding whether it's shared; finds the gentle note about meals in the alerts (it links to Health) Finds the week view and says what they'd do about the note T9 Family chat "Tell James that Mom's Lisinopril went up to 20 mg." (Typed; see the reminder on chat voice.) Then: "Would you add Ana to this chat?" Reaction to the health-detail check: Save as a note, Send anyway or Edit; finds People; who they'd add and why Makes a choice on the check and finds where to add Ana

After each: "1–5, how easy?" and "Would this replace something you do today? What?"

docs.title: 8. Wrap-up (3 min)
docs.text:
• What would stop you from inviting the whole family and the caregiver into an app like this?
  • What would you pay, if anything? Who pays today for care tools?
  • Follow-up OK? Confirm incentive.

docs.title: Journey Maps (Hypothesis Journeys)
docs.text: Notion story: CC-5 Map current-state journeys for each persona Status: HYPOTHESIS JOURNEYS — update after interviews. These maps are assumptions written before any research. They are built from the personas and the problem statement, not from participants. Every cell must be confirmed, changed or deleted once CC-2/3/4 interviews are done.

docs.title: How to read these maps
docs.text:
• Each map is the current state (life without Circle Care), so opportunities are not biased toward existing features.
  • Rows: stage → actions → thoughts → feelings → pain points → opportunities.
  • Hypothesis IDs (H-E1, H-C3, H-G2…) link back to the interview guides.
  • Feelings are written in words (positive / neutral / negative plus a short descriptor), not icons.

docs.title: Journey 1 — Elder: Maggie, a regular weekday
docs.text: Stage Morning wake-up Medicines Aide visit Afternoon alone Something goes wrong Evening Actions Gets up; daughter calls "just checking" Uses a weekly pill box; sometimes forgets which day Aide arrives; helps with shower and lunch; writes in a paper notebook Watches TV, naps, short walk Feels dizzy; unsure whether to "bother" anyone Evening tablet; daughter calls again Thoughts "She worries too much." "Did I take the morning one?" "I could do this myself if my knees were better." "I don't want to be a burden." "It's probably nothing." "Another call. I'm fine." Feelings Neutral → mildly irritated Uncertain Mixed: grateful, a little embarrassed Calm, sometimes lonely Anxious Tired Pain points Repeated check-in calls feel like being monitored (H-E1) Double or missed doses; no record Doesn't know what the aide writes or who reads it (H-E2) Nobody knows she's OK unless they call Pendant not worn; hesitates to call (H-E5) Same questions every call Opportunities A one-tap "I'm OK" that replaces the call Spoken reminder + simple confirm with taken/skip/refuse (H-E4) Elder can see who sees notes; Privacy Center Passive reassurance to family without calls Phone SOS with hold + cancel window Weekly digest so family stops asking

"No news is… good news?" (H-G1) "Why didn't anyone tell me?" (H-G2) "Should I ask Mom first? There's no time." (H-G5) "I'm repeating myself to three people." "I don't really know how the week went." Feelings Anxious Distracted, guilty Frustrated, alarmed Pressured Drained Uncertain Pain points Daily calls irritate Mom No passive signal she's OK Late discovery; no escalation Decisions lack context; Mom left out Repeated updates; siblings second-guess No record; hard to talk to doctors Opportunities "Today at a glance" (H-G7) Alerts only when something is actually wrong; quiet hours Escalation timers (caregiver first, then guardian) (H-G3) Approvals with context; elder notified of every decision Weekly digest (H-G6); family role with limited access History and export

docs.title: Guardian side journey: proving authority (one-time)
docs.text: Stage Joins app Uploads POA Waits Verified / rejected Pain points (hypothesis) Unsure why proof is needed Scans are blurry; wrong document Wants access now (H-G4) Rejection without reason feels insulting Opportunities Explain why in one sentence Check file type and readability at upload (CC-67) Show expected review time; elder still protected meanwhile Clear rejection reason (CC-24 reasons list)

docs.title: Synthesis process (after interviews)
docs.text:
Run within 5 working days of the last interview, with at least 2 people.

  1. Prepare. Print or paste each de-identified note into a whiteboard tool. One observation per sticky: a quote, an action, or a pain point. Tag each with participant ID and segment color (elder orange, caregiver teal, guardian indigo — matching the app).
  2. Silent sort (30 min). Each person groups stickies by similarity without talking. No pre-defined categories.
  3. Name clusters (30 min). Discuss and give each cluster a sentence label in the participant's voice ("I don't know what the aide writes about me"), not a feature name.
  4. Count. For each cluster, record how many distinct participants and segments contributed. A cluster needs 3+ participants to be a theme.
  5. Check hypotheses. For each hypothesis (H-E, H-C, H-G*), mark supported / mixed / not supported / not tested, citing participant IDs.
  6. Look for contradictions across triads. Where elder, caregiver and guardian in the same triad describe the same event differently, write it down; these are design tensions (e.g., safety vs. autonomy).
  7. Update the journeys. Replace hypothesis cells with evidence; strike through cells that were wrong. Change the status line to "Evidence-based, v1 (date)".
  8. Feed CC-6. Move the top themes into the opportunity solution tree as opportunities; retire opportunities with no evidence.

docs.title: Synthesis output template
docs.text: Theme (participant voice) Segments # participants Hypotheses affected Example quote (de-identified) Opportunity

docs.title: Opportunity Solution Tree
docs.text: Notion story: CC-6 Build the opportunity solution tree Status: DRAFT v0 — opportunities are hypotheses drawn from the personas and CC-5 hypothesis journeys. Re-rank after CC-2/3/4 interviews and the CC-74 pilot.

docs.title: Desired outcome (North Star)
docs.text:
Verified care tasks completed on time, per circle, per week.

  • Care task = a scheduled dose or a scheduled care task (meal, shower, walk…).
  • Verified = confirmed in the app by the elder or a circle member, with a caregiver-verified flag where the dose was given during a visit (DoseLog.verified, CC-41).
  • On time = confirmed within the escalation window (dose: before the caregiver escalation at 30 min, settings.doseEscalation.caregiverMin).
  • Measured per circle, per week; reported as the median across circles on the pilot dashboard (CC-77).

Why this metric: it rises only when the elder is safer and the circle has less doubt. It does not reward sending more notifications or collecting more data.

Guardrail metrics (must not get worse): - Elder-initiated privacy actions that indicate distress (members removed, sharing paused for 7+ days) — watch, don't suppress. - Alert volume per guardian per week (alert fatigue). - Refused doses must be recorded honestly; a "refused" is not a failure of the metric — it counts as a verified task outcome.

docs.title: Competitive Teardown
docs.text: Notion story: CC-7 Competitive teardown of care-coordination products Status: DRAFT. All product facts below are "verify before publishing — as of training knowledge". They were written from general knowledge, not from hands-on testing, current websites or pricing pages. Products change, merge and shut down; someone must re-check every row before this is shared outside the team.

docs.title: 1. Teardown framework
docs.text:
For each product, a reviewer installs or demos it (where allowed by terms of service) and scores these dimensions. Do not create fake accounts that misrepresent who you are; use a personal account or vendor demo.

Dimension Question Why it matters for Circle Care Primary user Who does the product serve first? Circle Care puts the elder at the center, not the family or agency Circle model Can multiple roles share one person's care? Are roles different? Our role matrix (CC-18) is core Elder UI Can an older adult use it directly (large text, few choices, voice)? Three-button elder home (CC-68) Medication Reminders, confirmation, escalation to others? Dose confirmation + escalation (CC-39–43) Safety SOS / fall / check-in? Who responds? Hold-to-send SOS with chain (CC-46–48), daily I'm OK Paid-care workflow Shifts, visit verification, hand-offs? Caregiver shift mode (CC-54–60, CC-82) Guardian/legal Any verification of legal authority? Guardian verification (CC-23/24) Elder privacy control Can the elder see/limit who sees what? Access log? Privacy Center (CC-81) Notification privacy Do lock screens show health details? PHI-free notifications (CC-31) Business model Free/ads/subscription/B2B/device? Informs pricing and trust posture HIPAA posture Consumer app, BAA-capable, or covered-entity tool? See CC-8

Scoring: 0 = absent, 1 = basic, 2 = strong. Record evidence (screenshot reference or URL + date) for each score.

docs.title: 4. Positioning gaps Circle Care targets (hypotheses)
docs.text:
1. Nobody puts the elder in charge of the circle. Family tools (CaringBridge, Lotsa, Life360) are built for the family; agency tools are built for the agency. Circle Care's bet: the elder owns the circle, sees an access log and can pause sharing. Validate with H-E2, H-E3.
  2. Family tools and agency tools don't meet. Agency software verifies visits but families rarely see it in real time; family tools have no idea a paid caregiver exists. Circle Care's shift mode (pro@shift) bridges this. Validate with H-C6 and T8 in CC-6.
  3. Medication apps stop at the individual. Single-user med apps remind but escalate weakly, and don't distinguish a refusal from a miss. Circle Care records taken/skipped/refused and escalates caregiver-first. Validate with H-E4, H-G3.
  4. Medical alert is a device business. Pendant services offer professional monitoring Circle Care does not. Circle Care should not claim to replace a monitored alert service. Position SOS as "alert your circle," and consider partnering rather than competing.
  5. Legal authority is unverified everywhere. Most family apps let anyone call themselves "guardian." Verified guardian status (CC-24) is a trust differentiator — and an operational cost.

docs.title: 5. Threats and parity risks
docs.text: Risk Example Response A large family-safety app adds a "parents" mode Life360-style product extends to elders Lean on elder control and privacy story; they're location-centric Agency software adds a family portal AxisCare/WellSky-style family portals Partner/integrate rather than compete on EVV Free alternatives (group texts, shared calendars) Status quo Must beat on time saved (H-C1, H-G1), not features Medical-alert companies add family apps Lively-style Don't compete on monitoring; compete on care coordination

docs.title: Code review — Sprint 11: Accounts, Identity & Payments (CC-172 – CC-190)
docs.text: Branch feature/accounts-identity-payments → main Commits reviewed e8ef366 (feature), bc2a6f6 (review fixes) Approver Lead Architect Agent (independent AI review agent) Developer · Tester · Build & Deploy Dev Agent · QA Agent · Release Agent Product Owner Sumanth (PO) Date 2026-10-25 Final verdict APPROVED (after one round of changes)

docs.title: Round 1 — APPROVED WITH CHANGES
docs.text:
The reviewer confirmed these were sound: parameterised SQL with allow-listed columns, every payment query scoped to the user, vault tokens owned/single-use/expiring, the CSRF header plus a SameSite=Strict cookie, the service worker skipping the API, and production start-up guards.

# Finding Fix Regression test M1 Parallel wrong passwords could skip the lockout (read-then-write counter) recordFailure() uses one atomic UPDATE … RETURNING; the lock is set when the count reaches 5 20 concurrent wrong passwords → locked M2 The password step for changing an SSN allowed unlimited guesses Failures count toward the same lockout; a lock deletes every session and returns 429 5 wrong → 429, sessions ended M3 Non-prod accepted real ITINs (9XX-70-…) as "test SSNs" Non-prod rejects 9XX groups 50–65, 70–88, 90–92, 94–99 4 rejected, 4 accepted M4 A bank name containing 9+ digits caused a 500 (audit guard) Field validation rejects long digit runs; bank name removed from the audit detail Field error on bankName

Follow-ups also done: staging requires DATABASE_URL; Secure cookie in staging; Postgres unique violation (23505) → 409; malformed cookie ignored; live Stripe key refused outside production.

docs.title: Round 2 — APPROVED
docs.text: All four fixes and the follow-ups were confirmed by reading the code and re-running the reviewer's race scripts: 20 parallel guesses → failed_attempts=20, locked, correct password refused. Both TypeScript configs compile. 312 tests pass.

docs.title: Carried forward (not blocking)
docs.text:
• Production go-live needs the Stripe adapter (Stripe Elements for cards, Financial Connections or micro-deposits for the mandatory bank account).
  • Identity verification with a third-party provider; MFA, password reset and email verification for real accounts.
  • Shared rate-limit store for multi-instance production; "sign out everywhere" and rotating the session after sensitive changes.
  • Product decision: "mandatory" SSN and bank account are currently shown as Incomplete rather than blocking other actions.

docs.title: Code review — Sprint 13, CC-192: Fewer false alarms from the family chat health check
docs.text: Branch claude/project-thread-0da4wd → main Approver Lead Architect Agent (independent AI review agent) Developer · Tester · Build & Deploy Dev Agent · QA Agent · Release Agent Product Owner Sumanth (PO), go to build Sprint 13 given 2026-11-14 Date 2026-11-14 Final verdict APPROVED (round 5, after four rounds of changes)

docs.title: What changed
docs.text:
The family chat warns before a message with health details goes to the group. In Sprint 12 the check matched single words, so everyday phrases like "Stroke the cat" or "A dose of sunshine" brought up the warning.

  • phiHint() now blanks out known everyday phrases (EVERYDAY_SENSES) before it looks for health words. Anything not on that list still warns, so the check stays strict by default.
  • Each everyday phrase is spelled out word for word, with no free gaps, so it can't swallow a health word next to it.
  • "Stroke" still warns by default. Only its everyday senses are let through ("stroke the cat", "brush strokes", "a stroke of luck").
  • The star sign is matched on the original capitals ("Mom is a Cancer, birthday in July").
  • Curly apostrophes are read like straight ones.
  • No screen changed, so no Figma design was needed.

docs.title: Measured on a fixed test set
docs.text:
40 everyday messages, 40 messages with health details, and 43 mixed messages where a health detail sits next to an everyday phrase. All are part of src/__tests__/everyday.test.ts.

Before (main at 5576da5) After Everyday messages that warned 25 of 40 0 of 40 Health messages that warned 40 of 40 40 of 40 Mixed messages that warned 43 of 43 43 of 43

Acceptance criteria: every health message still warns, and no more than 2 of 40 everyday messages warn.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Heart rate stays strict. "My phone's heart rate app" still warns. A heart rate is health data whoever it belongs to, so a warning there is cheap and a miss is not. The story's refinement notes listed it as a false alarm; that note is corrected.
  • Warn by default, with a list of exceptions. A missed health detail costs more than an extra warning, so only phrases we've checked are let through. "The best medicine for her cough", "5 ml of cough syrup" and "a cancer survivor" still warn.
  • Unrelated test fix. gives the next dose when everything so far is confirmed failed after 9 PM because the demo data logs doses up to the real time. The test now drops logs after its own 19:30 clock.

docs.title: Round 1 — CHANGES REQUESTED
docs.text:
The reviewer confirmed these were sound: the global patterns reset between messages, curly apostrophes are read correctly, "a dose of sunshine and her dose of lisinopril" still warns, and the recap test fix passes at any time of day (checked at seven clock times). Every finding below was confirmed by running the check: each message sent with no warning, where main warned.

# Finding Fix Regression test 1 The car and device patterns had free word gaps that swallowed health words ("In the car her cancer diagnosis came up") Only "diagnose the car" as a direct object, or "the car needs a diagnostic"; the reverse pattern is gone still warns when a health detail sits next to an everyday phrase (4 cases) 2 The ml pattern let liquid doses through ("Give her 5 ml with juice") Needs a cooking verb and "ml of" an ingredient ("add 250 ml of milk") same test (4 cases) 3 "Prescribed course" let "prescribed course of prednisone" through Only "prescribed reading" (not reading glasses) and "prescribed route" same test (2 cases) 4 The star-sign patterns let real cancer messages through ("Is weight loss a cancer sign?") "Cancer sign" removed; the star sign needs a capital C, a person and a birthday word same test (2 cases) 5 Narrowing "stroke" to a few lead words lost real messages ("My stroke was three years ago", "Possible stroke") "Stroke" warns by default again; only named everyday senses are let through same test (6 cases) 6 "History test results", "dog surgery" without 's, and "Tylenol is the best medicine" got through "History" dropped; pets need 's; the idiom needs laughter, love, music, sleep or time same test (3 cases) 7 The test set never put an everyday phrase next to a health word Added the 24-message mixed set same test

docs.text:
All 19 round 1 examples were verified to warn, and all 40 everyday messages stay silent. Three new gaps, each confirmed by running the check:

Not blocking, for later: "Add 250 ml of milk for Grandma's soup" warns, which fits the design. Covid, strep, antibiotic and scan are not health words yet; that gap was already on main.

Both round 4 examples warn, and so do versions with a semicolon or a dash. "Add 250 ml of milk to the recipe" and "Add 30 ml of olive oil" stay silent with or without a full stop. docs.title: Code review — Sprint 14, CC-9: Data inventory and classification
docs.text: Branch claude/project-thread-0da4wd → main Approver Lead Architect Agent (independent AI review agent) Developer · Tester · Build & Deploy Dev Agent · QA Agent · Release Agent Product Owner Sumanth (PO), go to start Sprint 14 with CC-9 given 2026-11-15 Date 2026-11-15 Final verdict APPROVED (round 3, after two rounds of changes)

docs.title: What changed
docs.text:
• Every field of the demo state and every column of the Postgres schema has a data class in src/data/classification.ts: PHI, PII, sensitive financial or identity, or operational.
  • A unit test fails, naming the field, when a field has no class, a classified field no longer exists, or the data inventory lists a field under a different class than the code. It checks three sources: the types in src/data/types.ts, the live demo data, and the database catalog after the migrations run.
  • The inventory was rewritten from the code: where data lives, how SSNs, bank accounts, cards and photos are protected, which everyday features can hold health details, field tables, retention and open decisions.
  • The Privacy Center no longer says the access log holds no health details. It records who opened or changed what, and what can be a medicine or a document, so it is protected as health information.
  • No screen layout changed, so no Figma design was needed.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• The access logs are not operational. The circle's log names medicines, documents and appointments, so it is PHI. The server's audit detail keeps SSN, bank and card last fours, so it is sensitive.
  • Who and when go with the record. In a record that holds PHI, the member and the time are PHI too.
  • Readable ids are PHI. Demo ids embed what they are about (med-lisinopril, t-bath, s-ana). Production should use opaque ids; that is listed under the inventory's human actions.
  • Unrelated test fix. Three rules-engine tests failed after midnight UTC because "70 minutes ago" wrapped into today. They now pin the demo clock to noon. The real gap behind it, a late dose missed before midnight is never escalated, is filed as CC-199 with two to-do tests.

docs.title: Code review — Sprint 14, CC-195: Keep a change made just before the tab closes
docs.text: Branch claude/project-thread-0da4wd → main (PR #11) Approver Lead Architect Agent (independent AI review agent, encrypted storage) Developer · Tester · Build & Deploy Dev Agent · QA Agent · Release Agent Product Owner Sumanth (PO), go to start CC-195 given 2026-11-15 Date 2026-11-15 Final verdict APPROVED (round 3, after two rounds of changes)

docs.title: What changed
docs.text:
• The demo store starts an encrypted save as soon as the state changes (src/data/saver.ts), instead of after a 250 ms timer. Saves can finish out of order, so a save only writes when nothing newer is stored.
  • The latest state is saved again when the page is hidden or closed (pagehide and visibilitychange).
  • The 15 second rules tick keeps the same state object when nothing changed, so it doesn't save. A separate beat still re-renders screens that show the time.
  • Closing the circle (CC-33) pauses saving, drops any save under way and forgets the last state while the data and key are wiped, so nothing from the old circle can be written back.
  • The device key starts loading when the app opens, without blocking start-up. A failed key load isn't cached, and the wipe clears the cached key again once the key is deleted.
  • If encoding the newest save fails, it is retried once.
  • src/__tests__/saver.test.ts (12 tests) and the evening recap browser step (reload straight away, and hide then reload) cover this.

docs.title: Round 1 — CHANGES REQUESTED
docs.text: # Finding Fix 1 Must: a save under way during Close circle could write the wiped circle back Saving pauses during the wipe and saves from before it are dropped 2 Must: keeping the same state on a quiet tick stopped time-based screens re-rendering A beat counter re-renders them every 15 seconds 3 Should: waiting for the device key could block start-up if IndexedDB hangs The key load starts without waiting, and a failed load isn't cached 4 Should: one failed encode left the latest change unsaved The newest save retries once 5 Should: test gaps Tests for wipe, retry, hide, and the tick; hook-level rendering is not unit tested, since there is no DOM test environment 6 Should: the browser step waited a fixed time It now reloads straight away, then hides and reloads 7–8 Nits: security docs, and the unused saveEncrypted Threat model C2-I2 and the data inventory updated; saveEncrypted removed

docs.title: Round 2 — CHANGES REQUESTED
docs.text:
# Finding Fix 1 Must: save() still kept the last state while paused, so a page hide just after the wipe could save the old circle pause() forgets the last state and a paused save keeps nothing; new test for pause, save, resume, hide 2 Should: a key load during the wipe could cache the old key The wipe clears the cached key again after deleting it 3 Should: the hide-then-reload step doesn't prove the hide save by itself Step relabelled "nothing is lost when it is hidden first" 4 Nit: the system overview said the key loads before the first save Reworded

The reviewer confirmed the pause and resume order in Close circle is right, and that the beat can't cause a save or a loop.

docs.title: Code review — Sprint 14, CC-10: Threat model of the architecture as built
docs.text: Branch claude/project-thread-0da4wd → main Approver Lead Architect Agent (independent AI review agent) Developer · Tester · Build & Deploy Dev Agent · QA Agent · Release Agent Product Owner Sumanth (PO), go to start CC-10 given 2026-11-15 Date 2026-11-15 Final verdict APPROVED (round 2, after one round of changes)

docs.title: What changed
docs.text:
• The threat model was rewritten against the code on main. The October draft described a planned system with no backend. The new one covers ten components, from the web app to the Replit workspace, with 57 STRIDE threats.
  • Each threat names the code behind its control, its status (In place, Partial, Demo only or Missing), its impact and likelihood, the risk that follows from them, an owner and, where one exists, a story.
  • A unit test keeps the model honest as the code changes. It fails when a referenced file is gone or the named code survives only in a comment, when a row is malformed or missing, when a risk doesn't follow from its ratings, when a control names no file, or when a High risk that isn't in place has no story in the High risks table.
  • Six High risks have backlog stories: CC-200 (server sign-in second step), CC-201 (end every session), CC-202 (care data and permission checks on the server), CC-203 (verify the database certificate), CC-204 (shared rate limits) and CC-205 (deliver safety alerts from the server).
  • Stale claims in other pages were corrected: the server now sends the CSP and anti-framing headers, an accounts server exists, and a few data-changing actions are still unguarded.
  • No screen layout changed, so no Figma design was needed.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Rated for a production launch. Today's data is fictional or test-only, so every risk is rated for what the gap would cost with real people.
  • Risk follows from two ratings. Impact and likelihood are scored 3, 2 or 1 and multiplied: 6 or more is High, 3 or 4 is Medium. This made three browser-only gaps High (off-shift browsing, the inactivity lock, export), all under CC-202.
  • Alert delivery is in scope. Real push and SMS providers aren't built, but an alert that never leaves the elder's device is the biggest availability risk, so it has its own story (CC-205).
  • The public wiki publishes this model. Whether security documents stay public is left to the PO (C9-I1).
  • Still needs people. The model is agent-written and agent-reviewed. It still needs an engineer with security experience and the security officer (CC-79).

docs.title: Threat Model (STRIDE): Circle Care as built
docs.text:
Notion story: CC-10 Threat model for MVP architecture Status: DRAFT v3, reviewed against main (cc3e577) on 2026-11-15. It replaces the October 19 draft, which was written against a planned architecture and said the prototype had no backend. v3 adds availability threats and the Lead Architect's corrections. C8-T1 was updated on 2026-11-15 when CC-198 locked down the Browser tests workflow.

Still needs human security review

This model was written and checked by the build team's agents. Before any real data is used, it still needs review by an engineer with security experience and sign-off by the designated security officer (CC-79). It is not a penetration test (CC-78).

All care data in Circle Care today is fictional (the browser demo). The accounts server accepts real names, emails and phone numbers, but outside production it refuses real SSNs, bank accounts and cards (CC-182). Risks below are rated for a production launch with real people, which is what the gaps would cost then.

docs.title: 1. Scope
docs.text:
In scope, as built on main:

ID Component What it is C1 Web app React PWA (src/), service worker (public/sw.js), production CSP, served by the host as static files (server/index.ts) C2 Demo store Care-circle data, alerts, permission checks, access log, files and export, all in the browser (src/data/store.tsx, src/lib/secureStorage.ts) C3 Express API Accounts, profile, SSN and photo routes (server/app.ts, server/account.ts) C4 Sign-in, sessions and MFA Passwords, lockout, session cookies (server/auth.ts); the MFA step exists only in the browser demo C5 Postgres Persona tables, sessions, payment tokens, audit table (server/migrations/001_init.sql, server/db.ts) C6 Payment vault Simulated vault outside production and the payment-method routes (server/vault.ts, server/payments.ts) C7 Audit log and export Server audit events, masked views and the export command (server/audit.ts, server/cli/audit-export.ts) C8 GitHub Actions The Browser tests workflow on every pull request (.github/workflows/browser-tests.yml) C9 GitHub Pages This wiki, published by hand with mkdocs gh-deploy C10 Hosting and config Replit workspace and autoscale deploy running APP_ENV=staging (.replit), environment keys (server/config.ts)

Out of scope: integrations not built (pharmacy, EHR, wearables), a real Stripe integration (production mode answers 503 for new payment methods), native apps. Real push, SMS and email providers aren't built, but alert delivery is in scope: today an alert never leaves the device that raised it (C2-D1).

docs.title: 3. How risks are rated
docs.text:
Each threat records its Impact and Likelihood, and the Risk follows from them. The threat-model test checks every row.

  • Impact: High means real health, identity or financial data exposed or changed, or a safety alert lost. Medium means account data or availability. Low means nuisance or information about the system.
  • Likelihood: how easy the attack is with the control as it stands. High: anyone can do it today. Medium: it needs an insider, a stolen password or some skill. Low: it needs several controls to fail.
  • Risk: score High as 3, Medium as 2 and Low as 1, and multiply. 6 or more is High (High with High or Medium), 3 or 4 is Medium (Medium with Medium, or High with Low), 2 or less is Low.
  • Status: In place (the control exists in code, file named), Partial (some of it exists, file named), Demo only (it exists in the browser demo but not on the server, file named), Missing (no control in this repository).
  • Owner: the role that fixes it: Dev Agent, Release Agent, Security officer (CC-79) or PO.
  • Story: for a gap, the backlog story that fixes it; for a control in place, the story that built or tests it. Blank when no story exists yet.

Code references are written `file:symbol`. A unit test (src/__tests__/threat-model.test.ts) fails if a referenced file is gone or no longer contains the symbol outside a comment, if a row is malformed or an ID repeats, if a risk doesn't follow from its impact and likelihood, if a control that exists names no file, or if a High risk that isn't In place has no story.

docs.title: C4 Sign-in, sessions and MFA
docs.text: ID STRIDE Threat Control in code today Status Impact Likelihood Risk Owner Story C4-S1 S A stolen or reused password opens a guardian account that holds an SSN and bank details The server has no second factor. The six-digit step exists only in the browser demo with a fixed code (src/pages/SignIn.tsx:482913) Missing High High High Dev Agent CC-200 C4-S2 S Password guessing across many tries or many server instances scrypt hashing with N = 16384 (server/crypto.ts:N: 16384), below OWASP's minimum of 2^17; 5 failures lock the account for 15 minutes (server/auth.ts:const LOCK_AFTER = 5), and a per-address limit on sign-in and sign-up (server/http.ts:export function rateLimit). The limit is kept in each process, the deploy is autoscale, and the address comes from a forwarded header (server/app.ts:app.set("trust proxy", 1)) Partial High Medium High Dev Agent CC-204 C4-S3 S A session that was stolen, or used on a shared computer, can't be ended Idle 30 minutes and absolute 12 hours (server/config.ts:sessionIdleMinutes: 30); sign-out deletes the current session; session tokens are stored hashed (server/auth.ts:sha256(token)). The only path that ends every session is a lockout during SSN change (server/account.ts:DELETE FROM sessions WHERE user_id = $1). There is no sign out everywhere and no password change or reset, and an expired session row is removed only when it is presented Partial High Medium High Dev Agent CC-201 C4-I1 I Someone learns whether an email has an account For an unknown email sign-in still runs a password hash (server/auth.ts:await verifyPassword(password, await dummyHash())), so the message is the same. A wrong password for a real account also records a failure (two writes and an audit event), so timing differs a little. Sign-up answers 409 for an existing email, and a locked account answers 429 Partial Medium Medium Medium Dev Agent C4-D1 D An attacker locks a guardian out on purpose before an emergency Lockout lasts 15 minutes and is per account (server/auth.ts:attempts >= LOCK_AFTER), so anyone who knows the email can trigger it; SOS in the demo needs no sign-in Partial Medium Medium Medium Security officer C4-I2 I The session cookie is sent over plain HTTP Secure is set in production and staging (server/auth.ts:parts.push("Secure")); HSTS is sent in production only (server/app.ts:Strict-Transport-Security) Partial Medium Low Low Release Agent

docs.title: C5 Postgres
docs.text: ID STRIDE Threat Control in code today Status Impact Likelihood Risk Owner Story C5-I1 I Someone between the app and the database reads or changes data The connection uses TLS but doesn't verify the server's certificate (server/db.ts:rejectUnauthorized: false) Missing High Medium High Dev Agent CC-203 C5-I2 I A database copy or backup exposes SSNs and photos SSNs and photos are encrypted with AES-256-GCM under a 32-byte key from the environment (server/crypto.ts:aes-256-gcm); SSN lookups use an HMAC under a separate key. Names, emails and phones are plain text, the ciphertext isn't bound to its row, and there is no re-encryption tool for key rotation Partial High Low Medium Security officer CC-26 C5-E1 E The app's database user can change or empty the audit table A trigger blocks UPDATE and DELETE on audit_events (server/migrations/001_init.sql:audit_events_no_change). No roles or grants are created, so the app's user owns the tables and could TRUNCATE them or drop the trigger Partial Medium Medium Medium Release Agent C5-T1 T A bad value is written straight to the database CHECK constraints keep last-four columns to four digits and photos under 2 MB (server/migrations/001_init.sql:CHECK (ssn_last4 ~ '^[0-9]{4}$'), server/migrations/001_init.sql:CHECK (size_bytes <= 2097152)) In place Low Low Low Dev Agent

docs.title: C6 Payment vault
docs.text: ID STRIDE Threat Control in code today Status Impact Likelihood Risk Owner Story C6-I1 I A full card or bank number is stored Only tokens, brand or bank name, type, expiry and last four are written, and the last-four columns can't hold more than four digits (server/migrations/001_init.sql:CHECK (last4 ~ '^[0-9]{4}$')). vault_tokens.metadata (jsonb) and holder_name have no such limit Partial High Low Medium Dev Agent C6-E1 E The simulated vault is reachable in production It is mounted only outside production with the simulated provider (server/app.ts:paymentProvider === "simulated"); production needs a live Stripe key (server/config.ts:sk_live_) In place High Low Medium Release Agent C6-T1 T A vault token is reused or claimed by another account Tokens are checked for owner, kind, a 15-minute age, single use and revocation under a row lock (server/payments.ts:FOR UPDATE) In place Medium Low Low Dev Agent C6-I2 I Card numbers pass through the app server Outside production the simulated vault runs in the same process (server/app.ts:app.use("/vault/v1", vaultRouter(d))), so full test numbers reach it. A real provider's hosted fields would keep them off the server, but that integration isn't built Partial High Low Medium Dev Agent

docs.title: C7 Audit log and export
docs.text: ID STRIDE Threat Control in code today Status Impact Likelihood Risk Owner Story C7-R1 R A person denies a sign-in or a change to identity or payment details Events for each such action with actor and time (server/audit.ts:AuditAction); details that look like an SSN or long number are refused (server/audit.ts:LOOKS_SENSITIVE). No IP address or device is recorded, and failed sign-ins for unknown emails aren't recorded Partial Medium Medium Medium Dev Agent C7-I1 I An audit export leaks identity or payment data By default the export reads the masked views, rescans its output and records a SHA-256 of each file (server/cli/audit-export.ts:createHash("sha256")). With --full-names it reads names from the base persona tables (server/cli/audit-export.ts:opts.fullNames); no read-only auditor role exists though the migration calls for one; and mode 600 applies only to new files (server/cli/audit-export.ts:mode: 0o600), so an overwritten export keeps its old permissions Partial High Low Medium Security officer CC-184 C7-S1 S Anyone with database credentials runs an export under any name The operator's name is whatever is typed (server/cli/audit-export.ts:opts.operator); there is no access check beyond the database login Partial Medium Medium Medium Security officer

docs.title: C8 GitHub Actions
docs.text: ID STRIDE Threat Control in code today Status Impact Likelihood Risk Owner Story C8-E1 E A pull request's code gets write access or secrets The workflow runs on pull_request (not pull_request_target) with a read-only token and no secrets (.github/workflows/browser-tests.yml:contents: read) In place Medium Low Low Release Agent C8-T1 T A changed outside action alters what runs Every action is pinned to a full commit SHA (.github/workflows/browser-tests.yml:actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1), checkout keeps no token (.github/workflows/browser-tests.yml:persist-credentials: false), and a unit test fails if either slips (src/__tests__/ci-workflow.test.ts:keeps no credentials after any checkout). A pinned release that was bad when pinned is still trusted In place Medium Low Low Release Agent CC-198 C8-T2 T A compromised npm or PyPI package runs in CI or the build CI installs from the lockfile with integrity hashes (.github/workflows/browser-tests.yml:run: npm ci); Playwright is pinned by version without a hash. No dependency audit or Dependabot Partial Medium Medium Medium Release Agent

docs.title: C9 GitHub Pages
docs.text: ID STRIDE Threat Control in code today Status Impact Likelihood Risk Owner Story C9-I1 I The public wiki tells an attacker where the gaps are Everything under docs/ is published (mkdocs.yml:docs_dir), including this model, the code reviews and the risk analysis. No secrets or contact details were found; the PO's first name appears on several pages. Publishing is by hand after the PO's yes Partial Medium Medium Medium PO C9-T1 T The published site is changed to mislead readers No control in this repository: GitHub's own permissions decide who can push gh-pages, and no branch protection is recorded for it Missing Medium Low Low PO

docs.title: C10 Hosting and config
docs.text: ID STRIDE Threat Control in code today Status Impact Likelihood Risk Owner Story C10-E1 E Production starts without its protections The server exits without both keys, a database URL and a live payment provider, and refuses a live key outside production (server/config.ts:throw new ConfigError) In place High Low Medium Release Agent CC-183 C10-I1 I Real SSNs, bank accounts or cards land in a test environment Outside production only test values are accepted (server/account.ts:checkSsn(str(req.body?.ssn), d.cfg.testData)), and a refusal is logged by field name only (server/account.ts:action: "nonprod.blocked") In place High Low Medium Release Agent CC-182 C10-T1 T The deployed build differs from what was tested The Replit build runs npm install, not npm ci, so the lockfile isn't enforced (.replit:npm install && npm run build), and the server runs through tsx (package.json:tsx server/index.ts) Partial Medium Medium Medium Release Agent C10-I2 I The deployed copy is opened over HTTP It runs as staging, which sets Secure cookies but sends no HSTS (.replit:APP_ENV=staging) Partial Medium Low Low Release Agent C10-S1 S The dev server is reached from another site (DNS rebinding) The dev and preview servers accept any host name (vite.config.ts:allowedHosts: true). The dev server is also what the Replit workspace serves publicly (C10-I3) Partial Medium Low Low Dev Agent C10-I3 I The Replit workspace's public dev server exposes the dev API The workspace runs npm run dev (.replit:run = "npm install && npm run dev") on port 5000 mapped to port 80 (.replit:externalPort = 80). The dev API sends no CSP (server/app.ts:if (!opts.dev)), its cookies have no Secure, and its development keys sit in .data/ (server/config.ts:join(process.cwd(), ".data")). Only test SSNs, bank accounts and cards are accepted there Missing Medium Medium Medium Release Agent C10-I4 I Someone with access to the Replit workspace reads the encryption keys and database URL Keys come only from environment secrets (server/config.ts:key32("DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY"); who can open the workspace and its Secrets is set in Replit and recorded nowhere Missing High Low Medium Security officer C10-D1 D Behind more than one proxy, every user shares one address and one sign-in limit trust proxy is set to 1 (server/app.ts:app.set("trust proxy", 1)), which is right only behind exactly one proxy. Behind two, 30 sign-ins in 10 minutes from anyone would lock everyone out Partial Medium Medium Medium Release Agent CC-204

docs.title: 5. High risks and their stories
docs.text:
Threat Risk Status Story What the story's criteria require C4-S1 No second sign-in step on the server High Missing CC-200 Second sign-in step on the server for guardians and caregivers An authenticator app or passkey checked on the server before any session; hashed one-time recovery codes; the demo code never accepted in staging or production C4-S3 Sessions can't be ended everywhere; no password change or reset High Partial CC-201 End every session when an account may be at risk Sign out everywhere, password change and a 30-minute reset link each end every session; expired rows deleted daily C2-E1, C2-E2, C2-I1, C2-I2, C2-I3 Care data and permission checks run only in the browser High Demo only CC-202 Move care-circle data and permission checks to the server The API applies the permission matrix to every care record, checks invitations, shifts, unlocks and exports on the server, and separates the reviewer role C2-D1 Safety alerts never leave the device that raised them High Demo only CC-205 Deliver safety alerts from the server to the people who need them The server records and delivers alerts to each member's own devices, catches up after offline, escalates without the elder's device, and keeps settings and tells the person after a storage reset C5-I1 Database certificate not verified High Missing CC-203 Verify the database server's certificate Remote connections verify the provider's certificate; a bad certificate stops start-up in staging and production C4-S2, C3-I3 Rate limits per process, address from a forwarded header; no limit on SSN checks High Partial CC-204 Shared rate limits for sign-in and account changes One shared store for every instance, only the host proxy's address trusted, limits on SSN, profile, photo and payment routes, and expired buckets removed

Each story is in the Notion backlog as Needs refinement, with its full Given/When/Then criteria and a link back to its threat. None is in Sprint 14.

Two stories are marked Done for the browser demo only, and the server versions are the new stories: CC-12 (MFA) is covered by CC-200, and CC-19 (access rules) by CC-202.

Medium risks with no story yet, for the next refinement: contact changes without re-authentication (C3-S1), one shared CSP list for the build and the server (C1-I1), SSN squatting and its support process (C3-D1), account enumeration (C4-I1), deliberate lockout (C4-D1), database roles for the audit table (C5-E1), audit export access (C7-S1), IP or device in audit events (C7-R1), dependency checks (C8-T2), where security documents are published (C9-I1), deploy with npm ci (C10-T1), the public workspace dev server (C10-I3) and who can read the Replit Secrets (C10-I4).

docs.title: 6. What changed since the October draft
docs.text:
• Backend: the October draft said the prototype has no backend and payments were out of scope. The accounts server, Postgres, sessions and the payment vault now exist (C3 to C7).
  • Clickjacking (old I7): frame-ancestors 'none' and X-Frame-Options: DENY are now sent as server headers.
  • Guarded actions (old T1): most data-changing store actions call guard(), but acceptInvite doesn't, invite accepts any role, and the review queue has no route guard (C2-E1).
  • Tamper (old T4): a plain-JSON value is still accepted (C2-T1), and a failed decrypt resets the demo without telling anyone (C2-D2).
  • Export re-auth (old I4): the confirm step does nothing yet (C2-I3).
  • Reviewer (old I10) and guardian verification (old E1): any visitor can open the review queue, and can() doesn't check whether a guardian is verified (C2-E1).
  • View logging (old R1): views are deduplicated per resource across personas (C2-R1).
  • Availability: alert delivery, request floods, lockouts and the proxy setting are now modelled (C2-D1, C2-D2, C3-D1, C3-D2, C4-D1, C10-D1).
  • New areas: chat, check-ins, CI, the public wiki, the Replit workspace and hosting are now modelled (C2-I6, C8 to C10).

docs.title: 7. Human actions
docs.text:
• [ ] Review by an engineer with security experience.
  • [ ] Sign-off by the designated security officer (CC-79).
  • [ ] Decide whether security documents stay on the public wiki (C9-I1).
  • [ ] Decide who can open the Replit workspace and its Secrets, and record it (C10-I4).

docs.title: Incident Response Runbook
docs.text: Notion story: CC-34 Incident response runbook Status: DRAFT — not adopted, roles not assigned, tabletop exercise not yet run. Notification timelines must be confirmed with counsel; this is not legal advice.

docs.title: 1. What counts as an incident
docs.text: Any event that may have exposed, altered, or made unavailable circle data, or that stops safety features (SOS, escalation, dose reminders) from working. When unsure, open an incident — closing one is cheap.

docs.title: 2. Severity levels
docs.text: Sev Definition Examples Response start Updates SEV-1 Confirmed or likely PHI exposure across circles, or safety features down for many circles Database exposed; SOS delivery failing platform-wide; leaked export from many accounts Immediately, 24/7 Every 30 min internally SEV-2 PHI exposure limited to one circle, or a safety feature degraded Lost caregiver phone with an unlocked session; suspicious access confirmed; SMS provider outage with push working Within 1 hour Every 2 hours SEV-3 Security weakness without known exposure Vulnerability report; misconfigured log found with no PHI Within 1 business day Daily SEV-4 Questions, false alarms Suspicious-access alert that the guardian confirms was expected Within 2 business days On close

docs.title: 3. Roles (names TBD)
docs.text: Role Responsibility Primary Backup Incident Commander (IC) Owns the incident, decides severity, assigns work, declares closed TBD TBD Security lead Investigation, containment, evidence TBD TBD Engineering lead Fixes, rollbacks, restores TBD TBD Privacy/compliance officer Breach assessment, notification decisions with counsel TBD TBD Communications lead Messages to circles, partners, media TBD TBD Scribe Timeline log (UTC timestamps), decisions, evidence locations TBD TBD Counsel (external) Legal advice on notification TBD —

docs.title: 4. First-hour checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Open an incident channel and doc; record start time (UTC) and who reported it.
  • [ ] Assign IC and scribe.
  • [ ] Set initial severity (can change).
  • [ ] Safety first: are SOS and escalation still working? If not, tell affected guardians by another channel to check on the elder directly.
  • [ ] Preserve evidence: snapshot logs, do not delete or rotate anything yet unless containment requires it; export audit chain and run verifyChain equivalent.
  • [ ] Contain (see scenarios).
  • [ ] Identify affected circles, data elements (use CC-9), and time window.
  • [ ] Notify privacy officer; if PHI may be involved, start the breach assessment clock (discovery date matters).
  • [ ] Decide next update time.

docs.title: 5.1 Lost or stolen caregiver phone
docs.text:
1. Caregiver or guardian reports it (in-app or support).
  2. Guardian (or support, verified) uses Sign out everywhere for that member (CC-27). In the prototype this signs out all personas and alerts the guardian; in production it must revoke every server session and push token.
  3. If the phone was unlocked or the session lock was not triggered (default 15 min for caregivers, CC-14), treat as possible exposure: check the audit log for views from that member after the loss time.
  4. Consider temporarily revoking the member (Care circle → remove) and re-inviting on a new device.
  5. Device data is encrypted with a non-extractable key (CC-26) — note in the assessment, but don't assume it ends the analysis.
  6. Severity: SEV-2 if views after loss; SEV-3 if none.

docs.title: 5.2 Suspicious access alert
docs.text:
Trigger: rules engine alert — a member opened 8+ parts of the record in 5 minutes or had 3+ denials in 10 minutes (CC-35).

  1. Guardian receives "Circle Care security notice" with in-app detail.
  2. Guardian confirms with the elder whether the access was expected.
  3. If not expected: remove the member's access, then contact support.
  4. Support reviews the audit log for that member; verify chain integrity.
  5. Assess whether the member is an account takeover (spoofing) or a legitimate member over-reaching (possible elder abuse concern — escalate per policy; see CC-8 Q12).

docs.title: 5.3 Leaked export file
docs.text:
1. Exports are passphrase-encrypted (PBKDF2-SHA256 250k → AES-256-GCM, CC-32). Determine whether the passphrase was also exposed.
  2. Identify the export event in the audit log (exported), who exported and when.
  3. If the passphrase was exposed or the file was weakly protected: SEV-2, breach assessment.
  4. Advise the circle; consider changing whatever the export revealed that can be changed (e.g., emergency contacts) — health history cannot be "rotated".

docs.title: 5.4 Vendor breach
docs.text:
1. Vendor notifies us (BAA terms in CC-30) or we learn from news.
  2. Determine what data the vendor held per the register. If the vendor was PHI-free by design (push, analytics), verify with logs that no PHI reached them.
  3. Rotate credentials/keys shared with the vendor.
  4. Obtain vendor's incident report, scope, timeline.
  5. Breach assessment for our notification duties.

docs.title: 5.5 SOS or escalation delivery failure
docs.text:
1. Switch to fallback channel (SMS fallback exists in the design, via: "sms-fallback").
  2. Notify affected guardians to check on elders directly.
  3. SEV-1 if platform-wide.

docs.title: 6. Breach notification — confirm with counsel
docs.text:
Which rule applies depends on CC-8 (business associate vs. consumer app). Timelines below are general understanding and must be confirmed with counsel for every incident.

Regime Who is notified Timeline (general understanding) HIPAA — as a business associate The covered entity (e.g., the agency) Without unreasonable delay, no later than 60 days from discovery; BAA may set shorter HIPAA — covered entity duties (the agency's) Individuals; HHS; media if more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction Individuals: no later than 60 days. HHS: within 60 days if 500+; annual log if fewer. Media: within 60 days if 500+ in a state FTC Health Breach Notification Rule (consumer mode) Individuals, FTC, media if 500+ residents of a state Confirm current timelines with counsel State breach laws Residents, sometimes attorneys general Vary by state; some shorter than 60 days

A HIPAA breach is presumed unless a documented risk assessment shows a low probability of compromise (nature of data, who received it, whether it was actually viewed, mitigation). Document the assessment either way.

docs.title: 7. Communication templates (drafts)
docs.text:
To affected circle (guardian and elder):

Subject: Important information about your Circle Care account

On [date], we learned that [plain description]. The information involved may include [categories, no values]. We have [what we did]. You can [steps: review your access log, remove members, contact us]. We're sorry. Contact us at [contact] with any questions.

Plain language, large type, read-aloud friendly. Never include PHI in the notice email itself. Offer a phone call for elders.

To a partner agency (BA notice):

We are notifying you under our Business Associate Agreement of an incident discovered on [date] affecting [n] of your clients. Scope: [...]. Containment: [...]. We will provide a full report by [date].

Internal status update: time, severity, what we know, what we don't, actions, next update.

docs.title: 8. After the incident
docs.text:
• Post-incident review within 5 business days, blameless format.
  • Update this runbook, CC-10 threat model and CC-79 risk analysis.
  • Keep incident records at least 6 years (aligned with audit retention — confirm).

docs.title: 9. Tabletop exercise script (status: not yet run)
docs.text:
Duration 60–90 min. Participants: everyone in §3. Facilitator reads injects; participants say what they'd do and who they'd tell.

Time Inject Expected discussion 0:00 A caregiver texts support: "Lost my phone on the bus last night." Severity? Who verifies the caller? Sign out everywhere 0:10 Audit log shows 9 record views from that caregiver at 23:40 — after the shift ended Wait — pro@shift should block off-shift reads. Why did it succeed? (Policy bug or check-in never closed?) Severity up 0:25 One of the views was the emergency card (always shared) and one was a discharge summary Data elements involved (CC-9); breach risk assessment 0:40 The agency is a covered entity; this circle is under its BAA Who notifies whom, and by when 0:55 A local reporter emails asking about "a Circle Care data leak" Comms lead, holding statement, counsel 1:10 Wrap-up Gaps found, owners, runbook updates

Record: date run, attendees, gaps, actions. Not yet run — schedule after roles are assigned.

docs.title: Security Test Plan
docs.text: Notion story: CC-78 Security testing and penetration test Status: IN PROGRESS — internal checks done on the browser prototype (see §3). External pen test not yet commissioned. No production system exists to test yet.

docs.title: 1. Scope
docs.text: In scope (production, when built) In scope (now, prototype) Out of scope Elder/caregiver/guardian clients (PWA, later native) React prototype, production build in dist/ Vendor infrastructure (covered by their reports) API and policy engine (CC-19) Data-layer policy (src/data/policy.ts) Physical security Auth, MFA, sessions (CC-12, CC-14, CC-27) Device encryption, export, uploads (src/lib/secureStorage.ts) Social engineering of staff (separate exercise) Database, object storage, audit log (CC-28) Audit chain (src/data/audit.ts) Notification pipeline (CC-31) Alert titles Review console (CC-24) /app/review

docs.title: 2. Standards and checklist highlights
docs.text:
Target: OWASP ASVS Level 2 for web/API and OWASP MASVS (L1 + R where relevant) for mobile clients. Highlights most relevant to Circle Care:

Area ASVS / MASVS focus Circle Care specifics Authentication ASVS V2: MFA, lockout, credential recovery MFA for guardian and caregiver; lockout after 5 codes for 15 min (CC-12); passkeys/biometric for elder Session ASVS V3: timeout, revocation Inactivity lock (15 min default), Sign out everywhere revokes server sessions and push tokens (CC-27) Access control ASVS V4: deny by default, server-side, IDOR Every resource × action from the permission matrix tested at the API; pro@shift based on server check-in; IDOR across circles Validation ASVS V5 Upload signature checks + malware scan (CC-67); free-text fields rendered safely Cryptography ASVS V6, MASVS-CRYPTO AES-256-GCM, unique IVs, managed keys; PBKDF2 iteration count for exports reviewed against current guidance Error handling / logging ASVS V7 No PHI in logs or error reports; audit chain integrity Data protection ASVS V8, MASVS-STORAGE No PHI in notifications, URLs, browser history, caches, screenshots in app switcher (native) Communications ASVS V9, MASVS-NETWORK TLS 1.2+, HSTS, certificate pinning decision for native Files ASVS V12 Size limit 10 MB, type allowlist, signed URLs, watermarking API ASVS V13 Rate limits, schema validation Configuration ASVS V14 CSP as HTTP header incl. frame-ancestors, dependency scanning Mobile platform MASVS-PLATFORM Push payloads PHI-free; deep links validated (invite links) Privacy MASVS-PRIVACY No tracking SDKs; analytics PHI-free

docs.title: 3. Already done in this repository (prototype)
docs.text: Check Result Evidence Limits Content Security Policy Added to production builds via a Vite plugin that injects a <meta> CSP and no-referrer (vite.config.ts): default-src 'self', script-src 'self', object-src 'none', base-uri 'self', form-action 'self', connect-src 'self' vite.config.ts Meta CSP cannot set frame-ancestors, so the server sends the policy as an HTTP header with frame-ancestors 'none' (server/app.ts). style-src 'unsafe-inline' remains Dependency audit npm audit reported 0 vulnerabilities on 2026-10-19 Command output, re-run during this doc's preparation Point-in-time; add to CI Unit tests vitest — 180 tests passed in 4 files (policy, rules, audit, sha256) on 2026-10-19 npm test Tests the client data layer, not a server Permission matrix tests One test per resource × action × role, plus pro on/off shift, revoked users, pause sharing, reviewer src/__tests__/policy.test.ts Some store actions are not routed through can() — see permission matrix "Coverage gaps" Audit chain tests Tamper, reorder and removal detection src/__tests__/audit.test.ts Client-side only Accessibility audit axe-core WCAG 2.1 A/AA audit of 22 screens: 0 violations (2026-10-19, after contrast fixes) tests/e2e/a11y.py Manual VoiceOver/TalkBack pass still needed End-to-end tests 25 Playwright scenarios, all passing against the production build (2026-10-19) tests/e2e/e2e.py (Python Playwright; see tests/e2e/README.md) Not yet wired into CI

docs.title: 4. Planned internal testing (before pen test)
docs.text:
• [ ] SAST in CI (e.g., semgrep/CodeQL) and npm audit on every PR.
  • [ ] Secret scanning in the repo.
  • [ ] API authorization test suite generated from MATRIX (same approach as policy.test.ts, against the API).
  • [ ] PHI-leak tests: seed fake PHI and assert it never appears in push payloads, SMS bodies, email, logs, error reports, URLs.
  • [ ] DAST against staging (e.g., OWASP ZAP baseline).
  • [ ] Commit axe-core and Playwright suites; manual screen reader pass.

docs.title: 5. External penetration test — vendor selection criteria
docs.text: Criterion Weight Notes Healthcare / HIPAA experience High References from health apps Mobile + web + API in one engagement High Tester credentials (e.g., OSCP, OSWE, GWAPT, GMOB) Medium Named testers, not just company Methodology mapped to ASVS/MASVS High Willing to sign a BAA if testing touches PHI (prefer synthetic data only) High Test with fictional data like the demo Retest included High At least one free retest of findings Report quality Medium Ask for a redacted sample Cost and timeline Medium Must finish before pilot readiness gate (CC-74 §9)

docs.title: RFP outline
docs.text:
1. Company background and product summary (link CC-10 threat model).
  2. Scope: environments, URLs, apps, API docs, test accounts per role (elder, guardian, family, pro, reviewer), out-of-scope items.
  3. Objectives: authorization bypass across circles and roles, pro@shift bypass, session/MFA weaknesses, PHI leakage via notifications/logs, document upload abuse, audit tampering, review console isolation.
  4. Rules of engagement: testing windows, no DoS on SOS paths without coordination, synthetic data only, emergency contact.
  5. Deliverables: executive summary, findings with CVSS and reproduction steps, ASVS/MASVS mapping, retest report.
  6. Vendor questions: team, credentials, sample report, insurance, BAA willingness, price, schedule.
  7. Evaluation criteria (§5) and timeline.

docs.title: 6. Remediation SLAs
docs.text:
Severity (CVSS 3.1 / vendor rating) Fix by Pilot impact Critical (9.0–10.0) 7 days; hotfix Blocks pilot start / pauses pilot High (7.0–8.9) 30 days Blocks pilot start Medium (4.0–6.9) 90 days Track; risk-accept with owner sign-off Low (0.1–3.9) Next planned release / 180 days Track Informational Backlog —

Any finding that exposes PHI across circles is treated as Critical regardless of score. Risk acceptance requires the security officer's written sign-off and is recorded in CC-79.

docs.text:
• [ ] Commission the external pen test once a staging environment exists (not yet commissioned).
  • [ ] Commit axe-core and Playwright test files.
  • [x] Add CSP as an HTTP header with frame-ancestors 'none' (server/app.ts).
  • [ ] Add CI security checks.

docs.title: Permission Matrix
docs.text:
Notion story: CC-18 Define role permissions (matrix) Status: Implemented in the prototype (src/data/policy.ts, enforced through can() — CC-19) and covered by src/__tests__/policy.test.ts. Production server-side enforcement is not built: the accounts server exists, but care-circle data has no API yet (CC-202).

This page is a readable rendering of the MATRIX constant as of 2026-10-19. If the code changes, the code wins — regenerate this table.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Role Who (demo) How the role is decided Elder Margaret "Maggie" Lee Member.role = "elder" Guardian Sarah Lee, daughter, healthcare POA role = "guardian"; legal documents verified by review team (CC-23/24) Family James Lee, grandson role = "family" Pro — on shift Ana Rivera (home care aide), Ruth Okafor (respite, pending, access expires in 14 days) role = "pro" and a visit today with checkIn set and no checkOut (onShift()) Pro — off shift same people when not checked in role = "pro" only Reviewer Internal Trust & Safety review team actor id trust-safety → "reviewer"

Anyone not in the circle, or whose status is not active (pending or revoked), gets nothing (roleOf() returns null).

docs.title: Matrix
docs.text:
Legend: R read · W write · P propose (needs approval) · A approve · I invite · X revoke · E export · D delete · V review · S respond · — no access

Resource What it is Elder Guardian Family Pro on shift Pro off shift Reviewer meds Medication list R W R W R P R P — — doses Dose confirmations R W R W R W R W — — tasks Care tasks R W R W R W P R W P — — notes Care notes (everyone) R W R W R W R W — — notes.private Guardian-only notes — R W W W — — docs Care documents R R W R W R W — — docs.legal POA / guardianship papers R R W — — — V approvals Change requests R R A P P P — circle Members and roles R I X R I X R R R — schedule Shifts R R W R P R P R P — history Activity feed / check-ins R R R — — — digest Weekly digest R R — — — — audit Access log R R — — — — settings Circle settings R R W — — — — emergencyCard Allergies, conditions, contacts R W R P R R R — sos SOS events R W R S R S R S R S — data Export / close circle E D E D — — — — supply Pills on hand, refill requests (CC-120/121) R W R W R W R W — — wellbeing Daily check-ins: feeling, water, meals (CC-142/143) R W R ¹ — — — — chat Private family chat (CC-164/165) R W I R W I R W R W ² R W ² —

¹ Only while Maggie shares check-ins (settings.dailyLog.shareWithGuardian) and hasn't paused all sharing. ² Only once Maggie or Sarah adds that caregiver (state.chat.pros); switching them off, removing them from the circle or their time limit ending takes them out at once. Pausing sharing also takes family and caregivers out of the chat, like every other non-emergency resource.

docs.title: pro@shift — minimum necessary for paid caregivers
docs.text: The matrix uses a special rule, pro@shift, for anything about the elder's health or daily care. A professional caregiver matches it only while checked in to a visit today (onShift()): visit.caregiverId === actor && visit.date === today && checkIn && !checkOut. When the shift ends, access to medicines, doses, tasks, notes and documents ends with it. Off shift, a caregiver still sees what they need to do their job safely: the circle (who to call), their schedule, the emergency card, SOS — and they can propose schedule changes and swaps.

docs.title: Sharing paused — ALWAYS_SHARED
docs.text:
When the elder turns on Pause sharing in the Privacy Center (settings.sharingPaused, CC-81), can() refuses every action by family and pro roles except on three resources:

const ALWAYS_SHARED: Resource[] = ["sos", "emergencyCard", "circle"];

So emergencies still work (SOS and the emergency card) and people still know who is in the circle. The guardian keeps access while sharing is paused because they hold legal authority; the public FAQ says the guardian "is told sharing is paused." The elder's own access is never affected.

docs.title: Refused actions are logged
docs.text:
Sprint 12 actions live in src/data/everydayActions.ts and use allowed() from the store, which does the same check and writes the same denied entry.

Most change actions in the store go through guard() in src/data/store.tsx (recordDose, verifyDose, saveMed, requestMedChange, decide, task actions, sosAcknowledge, saveShift, requestSwap, reviewDoc, invite, revoke, settings, exported — exceptions listed under Coverage gaps): if can() returns false, nothing changes and an audit entry with action "denied" is written. Three denials by one person within 10 minutes raise a security notice to the guardian (CC-35). Read access in the UI is checked with AccessGuard / useCan, which call the same can().

docs.title: Notable design choices to review
docs.text:
1. The elder cannot read guardian-only notes (notes.private read = guardian only). This conflicts with "the elder owns her data" and may conflict with a right of access where HIPAA applies (CC-8 Q13). Product decision needed.
  2. The elder can read but not write circle settings (settings write = guardian). The store makes an explicit exception: the elder may change her own fields in ELDER_SETTINGS (textSize, highContrast, readAloud, sharingPaused, elderLockMin, emergencyCard, toured) without the matrix check. Confirm whether she should also control things like her check-in window and quiet hours.
  3. Family can write doses, i.e., confirm a dose remotely. Consider requiring presence or limiting to "taken with me".
  4. Approvals are proposable by an off-shift pro ("pro" listed explicitly), unlike meds/tasks.

docs.title: Coverage gaps (prototype)
docs.text:
Closed on 2026-10-19 for the actions below. The CC-10 threat model (2026-11-15) found three that are still open: acceptInvite has no check, invite accepts any role from the caller, and the review queue at /app/review has no route guard. The demo controls (skipAhead, simulate, resetDemo, persona switching) are unguarded on purpose. All of these move to the server in CC-202.

Action Check addNote, addDoc notes / notes.private write by visibility; docs / docs.legal write submitHandoff, acknowledgeHandoff new handoffs resource — write: pro@shift; read/ack: guardian, family, pro closeCircle data delete visitCheckIn professional caregivers only elderCheckin, elderAsk, elderSuggest the elder only sosResolve the elder (sos write) or a responder (sos respond) acceptShift the caregiver the shift was offered to acceptConsent the elder; or a verified guardian with a written reason

sosStart stays open so the presenter can trigger SOS in the demo; in production only the elder's device can raise it. All of these must still be enforced server-side.

docs.title: How it's tested
docs.text:
src/__tests__/policy.test.ts generates one test per cell: for every resource × action, it checks elder, guardian and family against the matrix, and checks the professional caregiver both on shift and off shift. It also checks:

  • unknown and revoked people get nothing;
  • pausing sharing limits family and caregivers to emergencies while the guardian keeps access;
  • only the review team can review legal documents.

Run npm test. On 2026-10-19 the full suite reported 180 tests passed across 4 files.

docs.title: Production enforcement (not built)
docs.text:
• The same MATRIX and can() must run in the API on every request (CC-19); the client copy is for UX only and can be bypassed.
  • On-shift status must come from server-recorded check-ins, not the device clock.
  • Reviewer access must be a separate internal app with its own authentication, MFA and audit.
  • Field-level filtering in responses (e.g., strip notes.private for non-guardians) rather than hiding in the UI.

docs.title: How to contribute
docs.text: This wiki is plain Markdown in the repository, built with MkDocs and the Material for MkDocs theme. Anyone who can open a pull request can edit it.

docs.title: Run the wiki locally
docs.text:
From the repository root:

pip install -r docs/requirements-docs.txt && mkdocs serve

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/circle-care/. Pages reload as you save.

Before opening a pull request, build in strict mode — it fails on broken links, missing anchors and pages left out of the navigation:

mkdocs build --strict

The built site goes to site/ (git-ignored).

docs.title: Publish
docs.text:
The site is published to GitHub Pages at https://sumanth1996.github.io/circle-care/ by the maintainer:

mkdocs gh-deploy

This builds the site and pushes it to the gh-pages branch. There is no automatic deployment.
