docs.title: Feature page template
docs.text:
Copy this skeleton for a new feature page. Keep every heading, even if a section says "None".

# Feature name

<div class="cc-meta" markdown>

| | |
|---|---|
| **Feature ID / area** | F-nn · Area |
| **Personas** | … |
| **Status** | <span class="cc-badge cc-badge--built">Built in prototype</span> |
| **Related stories** | CC-n title · … |
| **Last updated** | YYYY-MM-DD |

</div>

## Overview
## User journey
## Functional details & business rules
## Permissions & privacy
## Notifications
## Accessibility
## Data captured
## Edge cases & error states
## Test coverage
## Known limitations & production gaps
## Related pages

Status badges: cc-badge--built (Built in prototype), cc-badge--partial (Partially built), cc-badge--planned (Planned).

docs.title: Writing guidelines
docs.text:
• Audience: someone who has never heard of Circle Care. Define terms or link to the Glossary.
  • Plain English, no hype. Short sentences. Active voice.
  • Be accurate to the code. Quote UI labels exactly, in bold for buttons and italics for on-screen text. Check thresholds and timings in the source. If the wiki and the code disagree, the code wins — fix the wiki.
  • Separate today from tomorrow. Use "In the prototype" for what the code does and "In production (planned)" for what is not built. Never describe the prototype as production-ready.
  • Fictional data only. Never add real names, health details or contact information.
  • Admonitions: !!! note, !!! info, !!! warning, !!! tip. Use note for privacy points.
  • Diagrams: fenced ```mermaid blocks.
  • Traceability: reference stories as CC-n, and update the Traceability matrix when a page gains or loses a story.

docs.title: Screenshots
docs.text:
• Save as .webp in docs/wiki/assets/screens/, named area-screen[-variant].webp (e.g. guardian-home-mobile.webp).
  • Use relative paths and the figure pattern with descriptive alt text, a caption and lazy loading:
<figure markdown="span">
  ![Describe what is on screen for someone who cannot see it](../assets/screens/guardian-home.webp){ loading=lazy }
  <figcaption>One sentence on why this screen matters.</figcaption>
</figure>
  • Add class="cc-phone" to the <figure> for phone-sized captures; wrap two figures in <div class="cc-pair" markdown> to show them side by side.
  • Use fictional demo data, reset the demo first, and mention anything unusual in the caption.

docs.title: Naming conventions
docs.text: Item Convention Example Page files lower-case, hyphenated caregiver-shifts-and-handoffs.md Feature IDs F-nn in catalogue order F-05 Story IDs CC-n as in Notion CC-58 Release labels vN for prototype increments; Release N for roadmap releases v0.4, Release 3 Personas Elder, Caregiver (professional), Family, Legal guardian, Review team — Code references Path from src/ in monospace src/data/policy.ts

docs.title: Review process
docs.text:
1. Create a branch and make your change.
  2. Run mkdocs build --strict until it passes with no warnings.
  3. Open a pull request describing what changed and why; link the Notion story if there is one.
  4. Reviewers: the Product Owner (Sumanth) approves every change. Changes to security, privacy or compliance pages also need review by whoever owns that area (security officer / counsel once appointed).
  5. Check accuracy against the code, tone, screenshots and links.
  6. Merge; the maintainer publishes with mkdocs gh-deploy.
  7. Update Last updated on each feature page you changed and add a line to the Release notes if behaviour changed.

docs.title: Delivery roles & check-in approval
docs.text:
Every story is delivered by a named team. Roles are recorded on the story in Notion (Developer, Tester, Build & Deploy, Approver, Product Owner) and in each commit message.

Role Who Responsibility Product Owner Sumanth (PO) Writes and prioritises stories, accepts the increment Developer Dev Agent (AI) Builds the story and its unit/API tests Tester QA Agent (AI) Runs the unit, API, Playwright end-to-end and axe suites; records results on the story Build & Deploy Release Agent (AI) Builds, pushes to GitHub, publishes the wiki, and closes the story and tasks with a comment Approver Lead Architect Agent (AI) An independent review agent that reads the full diff before check-in. Code isn't merged until it approves; the verdict is recorded in the commit (Reviewed-by / Approved-by) and in docs/reviews/.

The roles are AI agents working for the Product Owner; they're labelled as agents everywhere so nobody mistakes them for people.

Definition of Done for a story: acceptance criteria covered by automated tests, every suite green, axe clean, privacy review recorded for PHI/PII stories, approved by the Lead Architect Agent, merged to main, wiki updated, and the story and its tasks closed in Notion with a comment naming the commit.

docs.text: Field Value Owner Sumanth — Product Owner (CSPO) Version 1.0 Date 2026-10-19

docs.title: Research & Compliance
docs.text:
Working drafts for the backlog stories that need real people, counsel or vendors to complete: user research, regulatory and data-protection analysis, security planning and the pilot plan. They live in docs/research, docs/compliance, docs/security and docs/pilot and are indexed for GitHub readers in docs/README.md.

Drafts — not legal advice

Status as of 2026-10-19: working drafts. Circle Care is a CSPO-training concept product; all people in the prototype are fictional. Nothing in these documents reports real interviews, signed contracts, legal review or completed external tests unless it says so explicitly. Compliance documents are not legal advice. Each document starts with its Notion story ID and lists the human action still needed.

docs.title: Open findings
docs.text:
Findings that came from reading the code while writing these documents and this wiki. They are candidates for backlog stories.

# Finding Status Where discussed 1 Several store actions bypassed the permission check Fixed Oct 19, 2026 (new handoffs resource, actor checks) Permission matrix — coverage gaps 2 The elder cannot read guardian-only notes (notes.private), nor hand-offs; the Notes hint says she can Open — product decision Notes & documents 3 A <meta> CSP cannot block framing; clickjacking protection needs an HTTP header Open — production Security & privacy 4 No committed axe-core or Playwright scripts Fixed — 29 scenarios, 24 screens Quality & testing 5 The /pilot form collects name and contact but discards them; production needs a separate, deletable contact store Open Pilot & feedback 6 An unverified guardian is not downgraded to family access, although the Care circle page says so Open Care circle & access 7 The guardian has no way to remove a member, although the suspicious-access alert tells her to do so in Care circle Open Care circle & access 8 The elder and caregiver apps have no calendar screen, although the appointment form says Maggie sees every appointment Open Care calendar 9 Closing a circle in the prototype also discards the access log, although the UI says it is kept six years Open — production design Privacy Center 10 Maggie's age shows as 81 (website, emergency card) and 80 (birth year 1946, Health); SOS responder shows a non-San Francisco demo address Fixed in v0.4 Release notes v0.4 11 docs/security/permission-matrix.md lacks the handoffs, vitals and appointments rows and still cites 180 tests Open — regenerate the doc Security & privacy

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Story IDs match the Notion backlog (CC-n).
  • Hypotheses are labelled H-E (elder), H-C (caregiver), H-G (guardian).
  • "Demo" = demonstrated in the browser prototype with fictional data; "Prod" = production work not yet built.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
Future releases after the prototype. Every item on this page is Planned — none of it is built. The plan mirrors the Circle Care roadmap in Notion (phases P4–P7); dates are planning targets, not commitments.

Where we are

The browser prototype (v0.1 – v0.4) delivered the MVP stories and approved additions described in Features. The next step before any release below is a production foundation — a BAA-covered backend, real authentication and notification delivery — and the 8-week pilot described in the pilot plan.

docs.title: Release 2 — Native & Connected
docs.text:
P4 · Jul 12 – Dec 31, 2027. Move from a web prototype to apps people can rely on: native notifications that wake a phone, real health data, real medicine data, and the languages Maggie's neighbours speak.

Epic Feature Value Native Mobile Apps iOS & Android apps with critical alerts SOS and missed high-priority doses break through silent mode — the one thing a web app cannot guarantee Watch companion & health sync Real heart rate, oxygen, activity and sleep through HealthKit / Health Connect, replacing simulated readings Health & Pharmacy Integrations FHIR medication import Medicine lists come from the prescriber's record instead of being typed in, reducing transcription errors Pharmacy refill integration Refill status and pickup appear on the calendar automatically Patient-portal appointment sync Doctor and lab appointments flow into the care calendar Language Access Spanish, Chinese, Tagalog app experience Serves the largest non-English-speaking older-adult and caregiver communities in California Translated notifications & care content Lock-screen text, reminders and instructions in each person's language

Success metrics (proposed targets): ≥ 95% of SOS alerts delivered to the first responder within 30 seconds · ≥ 90% doses confirmed in pilot circles · ≥ 60% of circles with at least one non-English user active weekly (where applicable) · app store rating ≥ 4.5.

docs.title: Release 3 — Insight & Safety
docs.text:
P5 · Jan 3 – Jun 25, 2028. Use the data the circle already shares to prevent problems: trends instead of single readings, safer medicines, falls and wandering, and scams.

Epic Feature Value Proactive Health Insights Trend alerts Flags gradual changes (e.g. resting heart rate rising over a week) before they become emergencies Weekly AI health summary A plain-language weekly summary for the guardian — descriptive, never diagnostic Doctor-visit report PDF One-page report of readings, adherence and notes to bring to appointments Medication Safety Refill tracker & low-supply alerts Nobody runs out of a critical medicine Photo pill check Caregiver or elder confirms the right pill by photo Drug-interaction check Warns when a new medicine may interact with current ones Wearables & Fall Detection Wearable fall detection Automatic SOS when a fall is detected and not cancelled Inactivity monitoring Gentle check when there is no movement at unusual times Safe zones & wandering alerts Guardian alerted if the elder leaves an agreed area at unusual hours — with the elder's consent Fraud & Scam Protection One-tap scam report & guardian alert Elder reports a suspicious call or message; guardian is told Scam-awareness coaching Short, respectful tips on current scams

Success metrics (proposed targets): median time from abnormal trend to guardian review < 24 hours · zero missed critical refills in pilot circles · fall-alert false-positive rate < 5% · ≥ 70% of elders keep safe-zone consent on after 30 days · reported scam attempts acted on within 1 hour.

docs.title: Release 4 — Connected Family
docs.text:
P6 · Jul 3 – Dec 22, 2028. Make daily life easier for everyone in the circle — not only safer.

Epic Feature Value Elder Independence & Connection Voice-first assistant Maggie asks "What's next?" or "Call Sarah" hands-free (on-device where possible) Memory aids Gentle prompts for names, places and routines One-tap video calls Faces, not just voices, with the people she chose Daily feeling, hydration & meal check-ins Richer, optional self-reported well-being Caregiver Support & Workforce Voice visit notes Caregivers dictate the hand-off instead of typing Photo proof of care Optional photos for tasks such as wound care or meals Caregiver burnout check-in Early warning for overloaded family and professional caregivers Shift marketplace Fill open shifts from trusted, vetted caregivers Timesheets & invoices Hours from verified visits become timesheets and invoices Guardian Admin & Finance Care expense & benefits tracker Tracks costs and benefits such as Medicare or long-term-care insurance Legal & insurance document vault with renewal reminders POA, insurance cards and directives in one place, with expiry reminders Guided care-plan builder Step-by-step care plan for new guardians Care Access Services Telehealth visits Video appointments from the calendar Ride booking for appointments Book transport for medical appointments Family group chat Conversation for the circle, with the same privacy rules

Success metrics (proposed targets): elder weekly active rate ≥ 80% · hand-off completion ≥ 95% of shifts · open-shift fill rate ≥ 90% within 48 hours · guardian-reported time on admin down 30% · caregiver burnout check-in response ≥ 50%.

docs.title: Release 5 — Agency & Growth
docs.text:
P7 · Jan 8 – Jun 30, 2029. A sustainable business: home care agencies as customers and a family subscription.

Epic Feature Value Agency Accounts & Monetization Agency multi-client accounts Agencies manage many circles with role-based staff access Family subscription billing Paid plan for families with transparent pricing Agency caregiver compliance & EVV Electronic visit verification and caregiver credential tracking for Medicaid-funded care

Success metrics (proposed targets): ≥ 3 agency customers live · ≥ 25% of pilot families convert to paid · EVV records accepted by state systems without manual correction · gross revenue retention ≥ 90%.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text: Risk Release Mitigation Regulatory: FDA / clinical review for interaction checks and health interpretation R3 Use licensed, clinically validated interaction data; clinical advisory review; regulatory assessment before launch; clear "not a medical device" positioning where valid AI summaries must not diagnose R3 Descriptive language only, guardrails and human-reviewed templates, no treatment advice, visible "talk to a doctor" guidance, evaluation set before launch Critical-alert entitlement denied by Apple R2 Apply early with the SOS use case; fall back to time-sensitive notifications plus SMS/voice Integration access (FHIR, pharmacy, portals) slow or costly R2 Start with one EHR vendor and one pharmacy partner; keep manual entry Fall-detection false positives erode trust R3 Cancel window, tuning in pilot, elder controls Location features feel like surveillance R3 Opt-in by the elder, visible status, easy pause — consistent with the Privacy Center Translation quality for medical instructions R2 Professional medical translation and review; no machine translation of instructions without review Marketplace liability and worker classification R4 Legal review; vetted partners rather than a gig model EVV varies by state R5 Launch with one state aggregator; certify per state Monetisation conflicts with privacy promises R5 No advertising or data sales — ever (stated on the website)

  • Definition of ready: each epic needs a validated problem, success metric, privacy review and dependency check.

docs.title: Data model
docs.text: All entities are defined in src/data/types.ts and seeded in src/data/demo.ts. In the prototype the whole model lives in one State object in the browser. The data inventory (CC-9) classifies every state field and every Postgres column as PHI, PII, sensitive financial or identity, or operational, and proposes retention. The classes live in src/data/classification.ts, and a unit test fails when a new field has none.

docs.title: Computed, not stored
docs.text:
Vital-sign readings, activity, sleep, weight series, dose states, coverage gaps, streaks, adherence, North Star and the activity feed are all derived on demand (src/lib/health.ts, src/data/selectors.ts).

Since Sprint 12, src/data/everyday.ts also derives pills left, days left and the refill date (pillsLeft, daysLeft, refillPlan, lowSupply), Sarah's 7-day check-in view (sharedWeek), the no-meals note (mealsGap), who can read the chat (chatMembers), who is notified of a new message (chatAudience), unread counts (unreadChat), the chat's health-detail check (phiHint, CC-164, tuned in CC-192) and the evening recap (recap). Changes go through src/data/everydayActions.ts.

docs.title: Server database (PostgreSQL) — accounts, identity & payments
docs.text:
Since Sprint 11 (CC-189), real accounts live in PostgreSQL, separately from the browser-only demo state described above. The schema is in server/migrations/001_init.sql and is applied by versioned migrations.

The strategy favours testing the rules where they live (the data layer is pure and easy to test) and testing behaviour end to end for anything a person sees. A separate security test plan (CC-78) covers ASVS/MASVS and the external penetration test.

# Unit tests
npm install

# Type-check and production build

# End-to-end and accessibility (needs Python 3 and Chromium)

docs.title: CI
docs.text:
.github/workflows/browser-tests.yml (CC-194) runs on every pull request to main, on pushes to main and on demand: npm ci, npm test, npm run build, then vite preview and the three browser scripts, keeping tests/e2e/out/ as an artifact for 7 days. Each script exits with 1 on a failure, so the check goes red.

Since CC-198 the workflow runs Node 22 on ubuntu-24.04, pins every outside action to a full commit SHA with its release in a comment, keeps no token after checkout, and cancels an older run only for a pull request; every other run gets a group of its own, so runs on main always finish. src/__tests__/ci-workflow.test.ts fails if any of that slips. It checks that each pin is a full SHA with a release in its comment, not that the SHA matches that release, so when you update an action, look up the release's commit SHA with git ls-remote --tags and change the SHA and the comment together. Nothing updates the pins yet; Dependabot for GitHub Actions is in follow-up story CC-221.

Still to add: npm audit --audit-level=high, mkdocs build --strict for this wiki, and branch protection so a red check blocks merging.

docs.title: Security & privacy
docs.text:
This page explains the security and privacy controls that are real code in the prototype, how they work, and what a production system still needs. Detailed working documents: threat model (CC-10), permission matrix (CC-18), security test plan (CC-78), incident response runbook (CC-34), HIPAA risk analysis (CC-79).

Prototype, not a compliant system

The prototype demonstrates privacy-by-design with fictional data in one browser. Care-circle data lives only in the browser. The accounts server accepts real names, emails and phone numbers, but outside production it refuses real SSNs, bank accounts and cards. It has not been security-reviewed or penetration-tested and must not be used with real health information.

docs.title: Control summary
docs.text: Control In the prototype In production (planned) Story Encryption at rest AES-256-GCM in the browser; non-extractable key in IndexedDB Server-side encryption with managed, rotated keys (KMS); device encryption in native apps CC-26 Encryption in transit Care data: N/A (stays in the browser). Accounts API: HTTPS with Secure cookies; the database connection uses TLS without certificate checks (CC-203) TLS 1.2+ everywhere; certificate pinning in native apps CC-26 Authentication Browser demo: simulated password, 6-digit MFA with a fixed code, simulated biometrics. Accounts server: scrypt passwords, 5-failure lockout, per-address sign-in limit, no second factor yet (CC-200) Real MFA / passkeys, server rate limiting, device binding CC-11 – 13 Session management Browser: inactivity lock (15 min; elder optional), sign out everywhere (local). Server: hashed session tokens, 30-minute idle and 12-hour limits, sign-out of the current session; no sign out everywhere yet (CC-201) Server sessions with revocation, push-token revocation CC-14, CC-27 Authorisation One matrix and one can() check, called by most data-changing actions in the browser (gaps in the threat model, CC-10) Identical policy enforced in the API CC-18, CC-19 Audit Browser: SHA-256 hash-chained log with integrity check. Server: audit_events table where a trigger blocks changes and deletes, and a masked export command Server-side append-only log, externally anchored, 6-year retention CC-28, CC-29 Anomaly detection Bulk-view and repeated-denial alerts Tuned detection, security-team escalation CC-35 Notifications PHI-free titles Same, enforced in the notification service CC-31 Documents Content-type check, 10 MB limit, encryption, watermarked viewer Server-side malware scan, encrypted object storage CC-67 Export Passphrase-encrypted file (PBKDF2 → AES-GCM) Same, plus re-authentication CC-32 Deletion Wipe state, files and key on this device Deletion across services and backups (purged within 35 days) CC-33 Screen privacy App-switcher privacy shield Native secure-screen flags CC-26 Browser hardening CSP <meta> tag on production builds; CSP, frame-ancestors 'none', X-Frame-Options: DENY and no-referrer as HTTP headers from the server; HSTS in production only HSTS on every deployed copy; one shared CSP list CC-78 Voice On-device recognition only; nothing stored Same CC-73 Research data Kept apart from care data; health words scrubbed Separate store, retention policy CC-76, CC-77

docs.title: Encryption at rest
docs.text:
src/lib/secureStorage.ts (CC-26, CC-27):

  1. On first use the app generates an AES-GCM 256-bit key with crypto.subtle.generateKey(…, extractable = false, ["encrypt", "decrypt"]) and stores the CryptoKey object in IndexedDB (circle-care-keys). Because it is non-extractable, no JavaScript — including the app's own — can read or export the raw key bytes.
  2. Every save serialises the state to JSON and encrypts it with a fresh random 12-byte IV. The result is stored as enc:v1:<base64 iv>:<base64 ciphertext> in localStorage["circle-care-demo"]. A save starts as soon as the state changes and again when the page is hidden or closed (CC-195). Encryption is async, so a change made a few milliseconds before the tab closes can still be lost; real accounts are stored on the server.
  3. Loading decrypts with the same key. GCM authentication means a modified ciphertext or a missing key can't be read: the app starts a fresh demo instead, without telling anyone. A value without the enc:v1: prefix is still read as plain JSON (threat C2-T1).
  4. Documents are encrypted the same way in IndexedDB circle-care-files.
  5. If Web Crypto or IndexedDB is unavailable, the prototype falls back to plain localStorage (demo convenience only).

The e2e test CC-26 data at rest in the browser is encrypted checks that the stored value starts with enc:v1: and does not contain "Maggie".

Threat-model note

Browser-side encryption protects data from casual inspection of storage, backups and other origins. It does not protect against malicious code running in the page itself, which is why the CSP and a minimal dependency footprint matter.

docs.title: Tamper-evident audit log
docs.text:
src/data/audit.ts and src/lib/sha256.ts (CC-28):

hash(entry) = SHA-256( JSON.stringify([id, at, actorId, action, resource, prev]) )
prev(first) = "000…0" (64 zeros)
prev(n)     = hash(n − 1)
  • verifyChain() walks the log and reports the first entry whose prev or hash does not match — catching edits, deletions and reordering. The Privacy Center shows "Access log is intact — All N entries check out" or "Entry N of M doesn't match its seal."
  • Entries store ids, actions and resource names, never readings or note text. A resource name can be a medicine, a document or an appointment, so the log is PHI (data inventory).
  • RETENTION_YEARS = 6 documents the intended retention.
  • SHA-256 is implemented in pure JavaScript so the chain can be computed synchronously; a unit test compares it with Node's crypto for edge-case inputs.

Limitation: an attacker who controls the device can rewrite the whole chain consistently. Production anchors the chain externally (e.g. periodic hashes to a separate write-once store).

docs.title: Permission model
docs.text:
src/data/policy.ts (CC-18, CC-19) defines a role × resource × action matrix and a single check:

can(state, actorId, action, resource): boolean
Concept Rule Roles elder, guardian, family, pro, plus reviewer for the internal actor trust-safety Active members only Pending or revoked members, and unknown ids, get nothing pro@shift A professional caregiver matches only while checked in today and not checked out — minimum necessary ALWAYS_SHARED sos, emergencyCard, circle stay available to family and pros when the elder pauses sharing Health readings The guardian's vitals: read also requires settings.vitals.shareWithGuardian Enforcement Data-changing store actions call guard(), except acceptInvite, invite's role and the demo controls (see the threat model); refusals change nothing and write a denied audit entry. Read access in the UI uses AccessGuard / useCan, which call the same can()

docs.title: Content Security Policy
docs.text:
vite.config.ts injects into production builds only:

default-src 'self'; script-src 'self';
style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com;
font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com;
img-src 'self' data: blob: https://images.unsplash.com;
frame-src blob:; worker-src 'self'; connect-src 'self';
object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'

plus <meta name="referrer" content="no-referrer">. A <meta> CSP cannot set frame-ancestors, so the server also sends the policy as an HTTP header with frame-ancestors 'none', plus X-Frame-Options: DENY (server/app.ts). The two CSP lists are kept separately and must be changed together.

docs.title: Privacy shield and session lock
docs.text:
• Privacy shield (PrivacyShield in Extras.tsx): when the page becomes hidden (visibilitychange, pagehide), a blank cover with the logo replaces the screen so the app-switcher snapshot shows no health data.
  • Session lock (AppShell): after sessionLockMin minutes without pointer, key, scroll or touch activity (default 15 for caregiver and guardian; elder off by default, 5 or 15 by choice) a lock screen covers the app: "We lock the app after 15 minutes without activity so others can't see Maggie's information."

docs.title: Export encryption
docs.text:
encryptWithPassphrase() (CC-32): passphrase → PBKDF2-SHA-256, 250,000 iterations, random 16-byte salt → AES-256-GCM key → encrypt with a random 12-byte IV. The .ccexport file is JSON:

{ "format": "circle-care-export", "v": 1, "kdf": "PBKDF2-SHA256-250000",
  "cipher": "AES-256-GCM", "salt": "…", "iv": "…", "data": "…" }

Passphrases must be at least 8 characters and are never stored; "We can't recover it for you." The e2e test checks that a downloaded file contains AES-256-GCM and does not contain Lisinopril.

docs.title: Deletion
docs.text: Close this circle (closeCircle, CC-33) requires data: delete (elder or guardian) and a typed DELETE. It removes the stored state, deletes the device key (making any remaining ciphertext unreadable), clears the encrypted file store, records a deletion timestamp, and reseeds the demo. Sign out everywhere (CC-27) signs every persona out and notifies the guardian.

docs.title: PHI-free notifications
docs.text: Every alert has a generic title (what the lock screen shows) and a separate detail shown only inside the unlocked app. Titles in use: You have a reminder from Circle Care, Circle Care needs your attention, Emergency alert from Circle Care, Circle Care security notice, Circle Care health notice, and similar. The weekly digest email shows only counts. See Alerts & notifications.

docs.title: Anomaly detection
docs.text: Signal Threshold Action Bulk record viewing ≥ 8 viewed entries by one non-elder actor within 5 minutes Guardian security notice Repeated refusals ≥ 3 denied entries by one actor within 10 minutes Guardian security notice

docs.title: HIPAA posture
docs.text:
Circle Care is designed to the HIPAA Privacy, Security and Breach Notification Rules. Whether HIPAA applies depends on the business model:

Model Likely regime Consumer app used directly by families FTC Health Breach Notification Rule and state health-privacy laws Sold to home care agencies or providers Circle Care is a business associate; HIPAA applies and BAAs are required

See the regulatory memo (CC-8) — not legal advice.

docs.title: Server-side protection of identity and payment data
docs.text:
Added in Sprint 11 (CC-172 – CC-190). Details are on Accounts, identity & payments.

Requirement Control SSNs protected (HIPAA §164.312(a)(2)(iv), GLBA Safeguards) AES-256-GCM field encryption with a versioned key id; last four only in every response; HMAC fingerprint for uniqueness; re-entering the password is required to change it No card data held by Circle Care (PCI DSS) Card and bank numbers go browser → vault; the API stores tokens and last four only; the CVC is never stored No real sensitive data in lower environments APP_ENV other than production accepts only SSNs 900–999, routing 110000000, accounts starting 000 and published test cards; blocked attempts are logged by field name only Safe production configuration The server refuses to start in production without encryption and HMAC keys, DATABASE_URL, and Stripe with a live key; staging needs stable keys; live keys are refused outside production Audit-ready (FDIC / legal requests) Masked views + npm run audit:export (masked CSVs, manifest with SHA-256, export itself audited); append-only audit_events Sessions Hashed tokens, HttpOnly + SameSite=Strict (+ Secure in production) cookies, 30-minute idle and 12-hour absolute expiry, 5-attempt lockout, CSRF header check No PII in caches or logs The service worker skips /api and /vault; the API sends Cache-Control: no-store; request bodies are never logged

docs.title: What production needs
docs.text:
1. The same permission policy enforced in a server API, with field-level filtering of responses.
  2. Server-side encryption at rest with managed, rotated keys; TLS in transit.
  3. The audit chain stored server-side and anchored externally; 6-year retention.
  4. Signed BAAs with every vendor that touches health data (hosting, database, push/SMS/email, error monitoring) — vendor register.
  5. Real push/SMS delivery and iOS critical-alert entitlements.
  6. Identity and legal-document verification by a staffed review team in a separate internal app.
  7. Breach response — incident response runbook with assigned roles and a tabletop exercise.
  8. A third-party penetration test (OWASP ASVS L2 / MASVS) — security test plan.
  9. A designated security officer owning the risk analysis.
  10. HSTS on every deployed copy. The server already sends the CSP, frame-ancestors and the other headers; the staging deploy sends no HSTS.

docs.title: System overview
docs.text: This page describes how the Circle Care prototype v0.5 is built. It is a single-page web application. All care data, rules and permission checks run in the browser. Since Sprint 11, a small API server holds real accounts, identity and payment methods in PostgreSQL (Accounts, identity & payments); it never receives care data. Where a production design differs, it is called out as In production (planned).

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text: Concern Prototype choice UI React 19 + TypeScript, Vite build, lucide-react icons, hand-written CSS (no UI framework) Routing React Router 7 HashRouter (URLs like /#/app/guardian) so any static host works without rewrites State One State object in a React context (StoreProvider in src/data/store.tsx), updated immutably via structuredClone Business rules evaluate() rules engine, run every 15 s and after every change Everyday care (Sprint 12) src/data/everyday.ts (derived views) and src/data/everydayActions.ts (changes): refills, daily check-ins, family chat, evening recap Authorisation can() and the MATRIX in src/data/policy.ts Persistence Browser localStorage, encrypted with AES-256-GCM; key and files in IndexedDB Audit SHA-256 hash-chained log (src/data/audit.ts, src/lib/sha256.ts) Offline / install Web app manifest + service worker (public/) Charts Dependency-free SVG components (src/components/charts.tsx) Speech Web Speech API — synthesis for read-aloud; recognition only when on-device Accounts server (Sprint 11) Express 5 + TypeScript in server/; PostgreSQL through DATABASE_URL; PGlite (Postgres in WASM) when DATABASE_URL isn't set, in development and tests, never in production Hosting Replit autoscale deployment (.replit): npm run build, then npm start serves the app and the API

docs.title: State model
docs.text:
• One state object (State in src/data/types.ts) holds the whole circle: members, medicines (with pills on hand), doses, tasks, shifts, visits, hand-offs, SOS events, check-ins, daily check-ins, the family chat, approvals, notes, documents, appointments, health settings, audit log, alerts and settings. See Data model.
  • Updates go through update(fn): the state is deep-copied with structuredClone, the action mutates the draft, evaluate() runs, and React re-renders.
  • Actions (actions in useStoreState) are the only way to change data. Each guarded action calls guard(state, action, resource) → can(); refusals change nothing and write a denied audit entry.
  • Selectors (src/data/selectors.ts) compute derived views — dose states, next item, late check-ins, coverage gaps, streaks, adherence, North Star, activity feed.
  • Demo clock: clock(state) = now + clockOffsetMin so presenters can skip ahead.
  • Versioning: STATE_VERSION (src/data/demo.ts) = 11. loadState() in store.tsx discards and reseeds a stored state with any other version. See State versions.
  • Persistence: each change starts an encrypted save at once, with the device key starting to load when the app opens (src/data/saver.ts, CC-195). A save only writes when nothing newer is stored, and the state is saved again when the page is hidden or closed. The 15 second tick keeps the same state when nothing changed, so it doesn't save, but screens that show time still re-render. Closing the circle pauses saving and forgets the last state while the data and key are wiped, so nothing from the old circle can be saved afterwards. See Security & privacy.
  • Read logging: logView(resource) writes a viewed entry at most once per resource every 10 minutes.

docs.title: Rules engine
docs.text:
evaluate(state) in src/data/store.tsx is a pure function over the state draft. It runs every 15 seconds (setInterval) and after every action.

Order Rule Story 1 Dose repeat reminder at +10 min; caregiver and guardian escalation at their thresholds CC-39, CC-42, CC-43 2 Missed check-in: elder prompt after window end; guardian at +15 min CC-52 3 Late caregiver check-in (> 15 min) CC-57 4 SOS escalation step every escalationDelayMin minutes CC-48 5 Approval waiting > 24 h CC-64 6 Suspicious access: ≥ 8 views in 5 min, ≥ 3 denials in 10 min CC-35 7 Unusual vital signs (if shared) CC-86, CC-88 8 Low medicine supply: one alert per bottle to Sarah and Ana when days left reach refillAlertDays, until someone requests a refill; plus a refill entry on the Calendar 3 days before it runs out CC-121 9 Cancel the automatic refill entry of a paused or removed medicine CC-121 10 Daily check-in: one gentle reminder to Maggie at 7 PM, only if she logged nothing CC-142 11 No meals logged for 2 days: one note to Sarah, only while Maggie shares check-ins, from 9 AM, and only if she logged a meal in the 5 days before (private or unshared days never count) CC-143 12 Evening recap: one update to Sarah at 7 PM (catches up until 11 PM), unless she turned it off or it falls in quiet hours CC-191 13 Expire time-limited members (and take them out of the chat) CC-25

pushAlert() ignores an alert whose key already exists, which makes the engine idempotent. Full catalogue: Alerts & notifications.

In production (planned): the same rules run server-side on a scheduler, independent of any open browser, with delivery through a notification service.

docs.text:

Command What it does npm install Install dependencies (Node 20.11+) npm run dev Vite dev server on port 5000, all hosts (Replit preview); /api and /vault are served in-process by the accounts server (PGlite unless DATABASE_URL is set) npm test Vitest unit tests (app and server) npm run typecheck Type-check the app and the server npm run build Type-check the app and the server, then vite build into dist/ with the CSP meta tag injected npm start Run the accounts server (server/index.ts), which also serves dist/ npm run db:migrate Apply database migrations (server/migrations) npm run audit:export Masked audit export (CC-184) npm run preview Serve dist/ on port 4173 (no API)

docs.text: Status Meaning Built in prototype The user-facing behaviour works end to end in the browser prototype with demo data. Production hardening (server, real delivery, compliance) is still required. docs.title: Page template
docs.text:
Every feature page contains, in order:

  1. Header block — Feature ID / area, personas, status, related stories (CC-…), last updated.
  2. Overview — what it is, why it exists and its business value.
  3. User journey — numbered steps with screenshots.
  4. Functional details & business rules — tables of rules, thresholds and states.
  5. Permissions & privacy — who can see and do what, referencing src/data/policy.ts.
  6. Notifications — the exact lock-screen-safe wording.
  7. Accessibility.
  8. Data captured — fields written.
  9. Edge cases & error states.
  10. Test coverage — unit and end-to-end tests.
  11. Known limitations & production gaps.
  12. Related pages.

"In the prototype" always describes what the code does today. "In production (planned)" describes what a real deployment needs and is not built.

docs.title: Accounts, identity & payments
docs.text: Feature ID / area F-14 · Real accounts (/app/join, /app/login, /app/account) · API (server/) · PostgreSQL Personas Maggie (elder), Ana (caregiver), Sarah (legal guardian) — each with their own account and record Status Built — server, database, sign-up, profiles, photo, SSN, guardian bank account and cards. Payments run through a simulated vault (Stripe-ready); money doesn't move yet. Related stories CC-172 role picker · CC-173 sign-up · CC-174 sessions · CC-175 lockout · CC-176 – CC-178 persona profiles · CC-179 photo · CC-180 SSN · CC-181 SSN masking · CC-182 non-production guard · CC-183 production start-up checks · CC-184 masked audit export · CC-185 activity log · CC-186 bank account · CC-187 cards · CC-188 manage cards · CC-189 schema · CC-190 API & Replit Sprint Sprint 11 — Accounts, Identity & Payments (Oct 26 – Nov 8, 2026) Team PO: Sumanth · Developer: Dev Agent · Tester: QA Agent · Build & Deploy: Release Agent · Approver: Lead Architect Agent Last updated 2026-10-25

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
What. Circle Care now has real accounts. Anyone can open the website, pick who they are in the care circle — the elder, a caregiver or the legal guardian — create an account, and complete a profile: name, contact number, email, a photo and their Social Security number. The legal guardian also adds the bank account used to pay for care by ACH (no platform fee) and can add credit or debit cards, one of them primary. Everything is stored on the server in PostgreSQL, with elders, caregivers and guardians in separate tables.

Why. The earlier prototype switched between demo people and kept everything in the browser. A real care product needs real, verified people, and the guardian needs a way to pay. Because that means holding Social Security numbers and bank details, the feature is built around protecting them: encrypted, never shown in full, never present in test environments, and masked for audits.

Business value.

  • Turns the demo into a working product foundation that every roadmap epic builds on.
  • Identity verification keeps care circles limited to known people, which families and agencies expect.
  • No-fee ACH plus card payments prepares for paid care and subscriptions (Release 4–5).
  • Field-level encryption, tokenized payments and masked audit exports make HIPAA, GLBA, PCI DSS and FDIC/legal audit requests answerable.

The demo is still there

Explore the demo keeps working exactly as before, with fictional people stored only in the browser. Real accounts and the demo never mix.

docs.title: 1. Choose your role (CC-172)
docs.text:
From Get started in the site header, or Create an account on /app, the person sees three large choices: I'm the elder, I'm a caregiver, I'm the legal guardian. Each says in one line what that role does. Sign in and Explore the demo instead are on the same screen.

Step 0 — choose your role.

The next screens show the role badge and a step indicator: Account → Identity → Photo for the elder and caregivers, plus Bank account for the legal guardian. Change role goes back to the picker and keeps the name, phone and email already typed.

docs.title: 2. Create the account (CC-173)
docs.text:
First name, last name, contact number, email, password and confirmation, plus agreement to the Terms and Privacy Notice. A live checklist shows the password rules as they're met. Mistakes are explained next to the field, and focus moves to the first one.

Step 1 — account. The password checklist turns green as each rule is met.

docs.title: 3. Verify identity (CC-180, CC-182)
docs.text:
The person enters their Social Security number. It's hidden as they type (with a show/hide button) and formatted as ###-##-####. In test environments a yellow banner explains that only test numbers starting with 9 are accepted.

Step 2 — identity. In test environments only SSNs starting with 9 are accepted.

docs.title: 4. Add a photo (CC-179)
docs.text:
Choose a JPEG, PNG or WebP photo. It's cropped to a square, resized to 512 × 512 and re-encoded on the phone, which removes location and camera data before anything is uploaded. Skip for now is allowed.

Step 3 — photo, with a preview before saving.

docs.title: 5. Bank account — legal guardian only (CC-186)
docs.text:
Bank name, name on the account, checking or savings, routing number, account number and confirmation. The numbers go to the payment vault, which returns a token; Circle Care keeps only the bank name, type and last four digits. The guardian can't finish sign-up without it.

Step 4 (guardian) — bank account for no-fee ACH transfers.

docs.title: 6. My account (CC-176 – CC-188)
docs.text:
Photo, name, role and Profile complete (or a list of what's missing). Sections: Profile (edit name, phone, contact email), Photo (change or remove), Identity (SSN shown as •••-••-1234; changing it needs the password), Payments for the guardian (bank account, cards, add card, make primary, remove), Your care circle (open the role's app with demo data), and Security · recent activity.

My account on a phone. Payments: one bank account for ACH, up to five cards with one primary.

docs.title: 7. Sign in (CC-174, CC-175)
docs.text:
Email and password. A wrong password and an unknown email give the same message. After five wrong passwords in 15 minutes, sign-in is paused for 15 minutes.

Sign in — the error never says which part was wrong.

docs.title: Account and profile
docs.text:
Field Rule Message when wrong First / last name 1–50 letters, spaces, apostrophes, periods or hyphens "Use letters, spaces, apostrophes or hyphens" Contact number 10-digit US number in any format; stored as +1XXXXXXXXXX "Enter a 10-digit US phone number" Email Valid address; trimmed and lower-cased; one account per email "Enter a valid email address" · duplicate: "We couldn't create an account with these details. If you already have one, sign in." Password ≥ 12 characters, not containing the email name, not a common password Checklist item that isn't met Terms Must be ticked "Please agree to the Terms and Privacy Notice to continue"
  • The role is fixed once the account exists. Changing it is a support process.
  • Profile complete means: name, phone, email and SSN for everyone, plus a bank account for the legal guardian. Otherwise the API returns profileStatus: "incomplete" and a missing list (ssn, bank_account).
  • The sign-in email and the contact email start the same. The contact email can change in My account, and the sign-in email stays as it was.

docs.title: Social Security number
docs.text: Rule Production Every other environment (development, test, staging, Replit) Must be 9 digits, not all the same, not a known invalid number (e.g. 123-45-6789, 078-05-1120) ✔ ✔ Group 00 or serial 0000 Rejected Rejected Area 000, 666 Rejected Rejected Area 900–999 Rejected (never issued as SSNs) Required — the only numbers accepted 9XX with middle digits 50–65, 70–88, 90–92 or 94–99 Rejected Rejected — the IRS issues these as real ITINs, so test numbers must use middle digits 01–49, 66–69, 89 or 93 Same SSN on two accounts Rejected: "This number can't be used. Contact support." Same Changing an existing SSN Requires the account password Same

docs.title: Payments (legal guardian only)
docs.text: Item Rule Bank account Exactly one, required. Replacing it saves the new one in the same transaction that removes the old, so the guardian is never without one. It can't be removed outright. Routing number 9 digits passing the ABA checksum. Outside production: only 110000000. Account number 4–17 digits; must match the confirmation. Outside production: must start with 000. ACH fee $0 platform fee. Enforced in the database (CHECK (ach_fee_cents = 0)) and shown on screen. Cards Up to 5. Luhn-checked, brand detected as you type, expiry must be this month or later, 3-digit (4 for Amex) security code, 5-digit ZIP. Primary card The first card becomes primary. A new card can be made primary. Removing the primary card promotes the most recently added remaining card, and the app says which. Exactly one primary is enforced by a unique index. Test cards (outside production) Visa 4242 4242 4242 4242 · Visa debit 4000 0566 5566 5556 · Mastercard 5555 5555 5555 4444 · Mastercard debit 5200 8282 8282 8210 · Amex 3782 822463 10005 · Discover 6011 1111 1111 1117 Vault tokens Belong to the person who created them, can be used once, and expire after 15 minutes. Removing a card revokes its token.

docs.title: Permissions & privacy
docs.text:
Data Who can see it How it's stored Name, phone, email Only the account owner (the care-circle sharing rules still apply to the demo app) Plain columns in elders, caregivers or guardians SSN Nobody in full — not the owner, other members or staff. The API returns the last four digits only. AES-256-GCM ciphertext (ssn_enc), last four (ssn_last4), HMAC fingerprint in ssn_fingerprints for duplicate checks Photo Only the owner (Cache-Control: private, no-store) Encrypted bytes in photos; location data removed on the device Bank account Owner: bank name, type, last four of account and routing numbers Vault token + last four. The full number is never stored, even encrypted. Cards Owner: brand, credit/debit, last four, expiry Vault token + last four. The full number and security code are never stored. Activity Owner (last 20 events) Append-only audit_events with masked details
  • Card numbers never reach the Circle Care API. The browser sends them straight to the vault and the API only receives a token, which keeps Circle Care out of the heaviest PCI DSS scope (SAQ A once Stripe Elements is connected).
  • The service worker never caches /api or /vault responses, so personal details aren't left in the browser's offline cache.
  • Request bodies are never logged. The audit writer refuses any detail that looks like a full SSN, account or card number.

docs.title: Environments & test data (CC-182, CC-183)
docs.text:
APP_ENV Use Accepts real SSN / bank / card? Database Keys development (default) Local and Replit Run No — test values only Replit PostgreSQL if DATABASE_URL is set, otherwise embedded Postgres in .data/ Generated once into .data/dev-keys.json if not set test Automated tests No In-memory Postgres Random per run staging Replit Deploy No DATABASE_URL required Required (stable across restarts); cookies are Secure production A real launch, when approved Yes DATABASE_URL required Required, plus Stripe live key; the simulated vault is disabled

If anything required is missing in production, the server does not start and lists what's wrong. A live Stripe key is refused outside production. Every non-production screen that collects sensitive data shows the yellow Test environment — use test data only banner with the test values.

docs.title: Audits: masked export (CC-184)
docs.text:
For an FDIC examination, a legal request or an internal audit, an operator runs:

npm run audit:export -- --out ./audit-export --operator "Jane Doe"
# add --full-names only for a legal hold that requires full names
File Contents people.csv Role, name (first name + last initial), email m•••@domain.com, phone (•••) •••-1234, SSN •••-••-1234, created date payment_methods.csv Bank ••••6789 / routing •••••0000 / fee 0; cards Visa •••• 4242, credit/debit, primary audit_events.csv Every audit event with masked details manifest.json Time, environment, operator, masking rules, row counts and a SHA-256 for each file

The export reads only the masked database views (audit_people_masked, audit_payment_methods_masked). If a file would contain anything that looks like a full number, it refuses to write it. The export itself is recorded as an audit.exported event. An auditor's read-only database role should be granted only these views.

Tip

With the embedded development database, stop npm run dev before running the export, because only one process can open it. With DATABASE_URL this isn't needed.

docs.title: Data captured
docs.text:
Table Purpose users Sign-in email, scrypt password hash, role, lockout counters sessions SHA-256 of the session token, created / last seen / absolute expiry elders, caregivers, guardians One row per person, separate per role: names, phone, email, ssn_enc, ssn_last4 ssn_fingerprints One SSN per person across all three tables photos Encrypted photo, type, size (≤ 2 MB) bank_accounts, payment_cards Tokens and display details only (CHECK constraints stop full numbers being stored) vault_tokens The simulated vault's token register (last four only) audit_events Append-only trail (a trigger blocks UPDATE and DELETE)

See Data model and Security & privacy.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
Method & path Purpose GET /api/health · GET /api/config Health check · environment and test values POST /api/auth/signup · /signin · /signout · GET /api/auth/me Accounts and sessions GET/PATCH /api/me My profile PUT /api/me/ssn Set or change SSN (change needs password) PUT/GET/DELETE /api/me/photo Photo (raw image body, ≤ 2 MB) GET /api/me/activity Last 20 audit events in plain language GET /api/me/payment-methods · POST …/bank-account · POST …/cards · POST …/cards/:id/primary · DELETE …/cards/:id Guardian payment methods (tokens only) POST /vault/v1/bank-accounts · POST /vault/v1/cards Simulated vault (absent in production)

All requests that change data must send X-Requested-With: circle-care. Together with the SameSite=Strict session cookie, this blocks cross-site requests that change data.

docs.title: Security controls
docs.text: Control Detail Passwords scrypt (N=16384, r=8, p=1), 16-byte salt, constant-time comparison. Unknown emails are checked against a dummy hash so timing doesn't reveal which accounts exist. Sessions 32-byte random token in an HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict cookie (Secure in production). Only its SHA-256 is stored. Expires after 30 idle minutes and 12 hours absolute. Lockout 5 failures in 15 minutes locks the account for 15 minutes. Failures are counted with one atomic database update, so parallel guesses can't slip past the limit. Wrong passwords on the SSN-change step count too; reaching the limit there also signs the account out everywhere. Rate limits Sign-up 10 per hour and sign-in 30 per 10 minutes per network; vault 30 per 10 minutes per user. Encryption AES-256-GCM with a key id in every ciphertext (v1.<keyId>.…) for rotation (DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS). Tampered data fails to decrypt. Headers CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', X-Frame-Options: DENY, nosniff, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, HSTS in production, Cache-Control: no-store on the API. Uploads File signature checked (JPEG/PNG/WebP). The Content-Type header isn't trusted. 2 MB limit.

docs.title: Accessibility
docs.text:
• Every field has a visible label. Errors are linked with aria-describedby, announced, and focus moves to the first one.
  • Role choices and all buttons are at least 48 px tall and work by keyboard. The step indicator uses aria-current="step".
  • The masked SSN is read as "Social Security number ending in 1 2 3 4".
  • All new screens pass the axe WCAG 2.1 AA audit: /app/join, /app/join/guardian, /app/login, /app/account with the card form open. Layouts work at 375 px with no sideways scrolling.

docs.title: Test coverage
docs.text: Suite What it proves server/__tests__/api.test.ts (81 tests) Every sign-up rule, sessions and expiry, CSRF, lockout, profile isolation, completeness, photo checks, SSN rules per environment, duplicate SSN, re-authentication, tamper detection, bank and card rules, token ownership, use-once and expiry, primary-card rules, append-only audit, schema constraints, and regression tests for every Lead Architect review finding (parallel-guess lockout, SSN step-up lockout, ITIN ranges, bank-name digits, malformed cookie). It also scans every API response in the suite and fails if a full SSN appears. server/__tests__/config-and-export.test.ts (14 tests) Production and staging start-up checks, live-key guard, Secure cookie, HSTS and vault disabled in production. The masked export's contents, manifest and hashes, and that no full number appears in any file. tests/e2e/accounts.py (15 scenarios, Playwright) The full guardian journey on a phone-sized screen, elder journey, duplicate email, wrong password, lockout, cards, activity, profile edit. Also checks that the SSN and account number never appear in the page. tests/e2e/a11y.py axe audit including the four new screens

docs.title: Known limitations & production gaps
docs.text:
• Payments don't move money yet. The vault is simulated. Production needs the Stripe adapter (Stripe Elements for cards, Financial Connections or micro-deposits to verify bank accounts) and a BAA review. Until then, adding payment methods in a stripe environment returns "not available yet".
  • Identity is checked for format, not verified with a third party (e.g. an identity-verification provider). That is a follow-up story.
  • No MFA, password reset or email verification for real accounts yet. The demo shows the intended MFA design. These are the next stories in the Accounts epic.
  • Accounts aren't linked into a shared care circle yet. Explore the … app opens the role's demo experience.
  • The embedded database is single-process. Use Replit PostgreSQL (DATABASE_URL) for anything shared.

docs.title: Alerts & notifications
docs.text: Feature ID / area F-12 · Rules engine, alert centre and in-app banners Personas All — elder (banners only), caregiver and guardian (banners and Alerts list) Status Partially built — alerts are generated and shown in-app; push, SMS and email delivery are not built Related stories CC-31 PHI-free notifications · CC-35 suspicious-access detection · CC-39 repeat reminder · CC-42 dose escalation · CC-50 critical alerts · CC-52 missed check-in · CC-57 late caregiver · CC-63 channels & quiet hours · CC-64 approval reminder · CC-86 health alerts · CC-25 access expiry Last updated 2026-10-19

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
What. A rules engine turns time and state into alerts: missed doses, missed check-ins, late caregivers, SOS escalation, stale approvals, suspicious access, unusual health readings and expired access. Each alert has a lock-screen title that never contains health information and an in-app detail shown only after the app is unlocked. Alerts appear as a banner when they arrive and in the Alerts list (bell icon).

Why. Families are buried in messages; health details on a lock screen are a privacy breach waiting to happen. Circle Care is "quiet unless it matters" — and when it speaks, the lock screen says only "You have a reminder from Circle Care."

Business value. Trustworthy, low-noise alerting is what lets the guardian stop calling every day, and PHI-free notification text is a prerequisite for using third-party push and SMS providers.

docs.title: User journey
docs.text:
1. Something happens (e.g. a dose passes its threshold). Within 15 seconds the rules engine creates an alert.
  2. If the recipient has the app open, a banner slides in: Circle Care · now · the lock-screen title, and "Lock-screen text above has no health details. Tap to see more." Critical alerts are red. Banners disappear after 7 seconds.
  3. Tapping the banner opens the relevant screen.
  4. The bell shows an unread count. Alerts lists each alert with its in-app detail, "Lock screen showed: "…"", and the age. Alerts are marked read 1.5 seconds after the list opens.
Every alert shows the generic lock-screen text it would have displayed.

docs.title: Rules engine schedule
docs.text: evaluate(state) in src/data/store.tsx runs every 15 seconds while the app is open and after every change. Alerts are de-duplicated by key, so a rule fires once per condition (per dose slot per day, per SOS step, per 10-minute window for security rules).

docs.title: Alert catalogue
docs.text:
# Alert Rule To Severity Lock-screen title 1 Dose repeat reminder Unconfirmed dose ≥ 10 min past time Elder Info You have a reminder from Circle Care 2 Dose — caregiver ≥ 30 min (15 high-priority) Caregiver Warning / Critical* You have a reminder from Circle Care 3 Dose — guardian ≥ 60 min (30 high-priority) Guardian Warning / Critical* Circle Care needs your attention 4 Check-in — elder No check-in after window end (10:00) Elder Info You have a reminder from Circle Care 5 Check-in — guardian Window end + 15 min Guardian Warning Circle Care needs your attention 6 Late caregiver Shift start + 15 min, no check-in Guardian, caregiver Warning Circle Care needs your attention 7 SOS sent Elder sends SOS Guardian, caregiver Critical Emergency alert from Circle Care 8 SOS escalation Every 2 min until acknowledged Guardian, caregiver Critical Emergency alert from Circle Care 9 SOS acknowledged Responder taps I'm on my way Elder, guardian, caregiver Info Update from Circle Care 10 Approval reminder Pending > 24 hours Guardian Info You have a reminder from Circle Care 11 Bulk access ≥ 8 record views by one person (not the elder) in 5 min Guardian Warning Circle Care security notice 12 Repeated denials ≥ 3 refused actions by one person in 10 min Guardian Warning Circle Care security notice 13 Unusual health reading Detection rules, only if Maggie shares Guardian Warning (high/low) · Info (sudden) Circle Care health notice 14 Access expired expiresOn < today — (audit entry only) — — 15 MFA lockout 5 wrong codes The person Warning Circle Care security notice 16 Evening recap (CC-191) Once a day at 19:00 (catches up until 23:00 if the app first runs later, never inside quiet hours), unless Sarah turned it off or quiet hours cover 19:00. In-app text: "Your evening recap is ready." Guardian Info Update from Circle Care

* Critical when the medicine is high-priority.

Action-driven alerts (new requests, decisions, invitations, shift offers, appointments, sharing changes, legal-document review) are listed on each feature page under Notifications.

docs.title: Lock-screen titles in use
docs.text:
Title Used for You have a reminder from Circle Care Reminders to the elder; dose reminders to the caregiver; approval reminders Circle Care needs your attention Escalations to the guardian (dose, check-in, late caregiver) Emergency alert from Circle Care SOS Circle Care security notice Suspicious access, MFA lockout Circle Care health notice Unusual readings You have a new request in Circle Care Change, member and swap requests You have a new message in Circle Care Elder questions and suggestions You have a new shift in Circle Care Shift offers You have an update in Circle Care Decisions, escort requests Update from Circle Care Informational updates

PHI-free by design (CC-31)

docs.title: Care calendar
docs.text: Feature ID / area F-08 · Medication-related appointments (/app/guardian/calendar) Personas Sarah (plans), Ana and James (escorts), Maggie (is told about new appointments) Status Built in prototype Related stories CC-94 – CC-98 medication appointment calendar — month view (CC-94), add / edit (CC-96), appointment types (CC-98); CC-95 and CC-97 are covered by the same range comment in code, with titles in Notion Last updated 2026-10-19

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
What. A full-month calendar of appointments that relate to Maggie's medicines: doctor visits, pharmacy refills, lab tests and medication reviews. Each appointment records who it is with, where, which medicines it concerns, who is taking Maggie, and how to prepare. An Up next banner keeps the next few appointments in view.

Why. Medication safety depends on more than doses: refills must be picked up, fasting lab tests must be prepared for, and follow-ups must have someone to drive. These usually live in one person's head or phone.

Business value. Reduces missed refills and appointments, and links each appointment to the medicines it concerns — the foundation for Release 2 patient-portal appointment sync and pharmacy refill integration.

docs.title: User journey
docs.text:
1. Sarah opens Calendar — "Maggie's medication appointments".
  2. The Up next banner shows the next appointment in its type colour: "UP NEXT · TODAY — Pick up Metformin refill — Monday, October 19 at 4:30 PM · Fog City Pharmacy · Ana is taking her" and the following two ("then A1c and kidney (in 2 days) · Diabetes follow-up (in 2 days)"). Tapping it jumps to that day.
  3. The month grid (October 2026) has Today, previous and next buttons and a legend counting this month's appointments by type (3 doctor visits · 3 refills · 1 lab test · 1 medication review). Each day shows up to three chips (icon, time, title) and +N more; past appointments are struck through.
  4. Selecting a day fills the day panel: type, title, time range, provider and location, About: Metformin, Ana is taking her, preparation notes, and Edit, Done (today or earlier) and Cancel.
  5. Add appointment (or Add one on an empty day) opens New appointment: type buttons (Doctor visit, Pharmacy refill, Lab test, Medication review), What, Date, Time, Length, With (doctor, lab or pharmacy), Where, Which medicines is it about?, Who's taking her? and How to prepare (optional) → Add to calendar — "Appointment added — Maggie will see it".
  6. On phones the grid switches to a compact view with coloured dots per day.
Month view with the Up next banner and the selected day's details. Adding an appointment. Compact phone layout.

docs.title: Care circle & access
docs.text: Feature ID / area F-09 · Membership, roles, invitations and legal-authority verification Personas Sarah (manages the circle), Maggie (confirms and removes members), invited helpers (Ruth), internal review team Status Built in prototype — identity checks and invite delivery are simulated Related stories CC-15 create a care circle · CC-16 invite by role · CC-17 accept an invitation · CC-18 role permission matrix · CC-19 single enforcement point · CC-20 who can see my data · CC-21 revoke access · CC-23 upload legal authority · CC-24 guardian verification (review console) · CC-25 time-limited access · CC-48 SOS escalation order Last updated 2026-10-19

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
What. The care circle is the set of people allowed to help Maggie, each with a role that decides what they can see and do. The guardian invites people by role, can make access temporary, and sets the SOS order. Maggie sees everyone and can remove anyone except her legal guardian. A guardian's legal powers depend on a power-of-attorney or guardianship document that an internal review team verifies.

Why. Shared family logins and group chats give everyone everything. Care requires the opposite: the right person sees the right thing, only for as long as needed, and the elder can see and change it.

Business value. Role-based, time-bound access is what makes Circle Care safe to recommend to agencies and acceptable to elders. Guardian verification protects against the most serious abuse risk: someone falsely claiming authority over an older adult.

docs.title: Manage the circle (guardian)
docs.text:
1. Sarah opens Care circle — "Maggie's circle". Each member shows a role badge (Elder, Legal guardian, Family caregiver, Professional caregiver), Verified for a verified guardian, Invite sent for pending invitations, the relationship, and "Access ends automatically Mon, Nov 2" for temporary access.
  2. For pending invitations she can copy the invite link or Open it.
  3. Who gets SOS alerts first lists the escalation order — "Sarah · immediately", "Ana · after 2 min without an answer", "James · after 4 min without an answer" — with up/down arrows. "Maggie can see this list in her emergency screen."
  4. Legal authority lists POA or guardianship documents with In review, Verified or Needs resubmission. In the demo, In review items have a Simulate approval button.
The care circle with roles, a pending time-limited invitation and the SOS order.

docs.title: Invite someone (CC-15, CC-16)
docs.text:
1. Invite someone → Invite to Maggie's circle: Name, Mobile number or email, Role (Family — "Sees today's medicines, tasks, notes and alerts." or Professional — "Sees today's plan only during their shifts."), How they're related (optional), and Temporary access with an Access ends date (default 14 days ahead).
  2. "The invite link works once and expires in 72 hours. The message contains no health information. Maggie is notified." → Send invite ("Invite sent to Lena Park"). The member appears as Invite sent.
  3. The invitee accepts at /app/invite/<id> — see Website & onboarding.

docs.title: Time-limited access (CC-25)
docs.text: 1. Members with an end date show it everywhere they appear. When the date passes, the rules engine revokes access automatically and writes "Circle Care removed Ruth Okafor's access (time limit ended)" to the access log.

docs.title: Remove someone (CC-21)
docs.text:
1. In her Privacy Center, Maggie taps Remove next to any member except Sarah → "Remove Ana? Ana will stop seeing your information right away, on every device. Sarah will be told." → Remove Ana / Keep Ana.
  2. The member is revoked, removed from the SOS chain, and listed under "No longer has access". "Sarah is your legal guardian. Her access can only be changed through the legal process, not in the app."

docs.title: Guardian verification and review console (CC-23, CC-24)
docs.text:
1. Sarah uploads a document of type Legal authority in Notes & documents. She is told: "We received "court-order.png". Our review team usually responds within one business day."
  2. A reviewer opens the internal Review team console (/app/review) — "Legal authority review". "Check that each guardianship or power-of-attorney document is genuine, current and names the person who uploaded it. Target: a decision within one business day. Reviewers can open only these documents; every decision is logged."
  3. Verify → the document and the uploader become Verified; Maggie and Sarah are told "Sarah's legal authority was verified."
  4. Reject → choose a reason the uploader will see → Reject and notify. Sarah sees "court-order.png couldn't be verified: It has expired. Upload a new copy as "Legal authority"."
The internal review console sees only legal-authority documents.

docs.title: Caregiver shifts & hand-offs
docs.text: Feature ID / area F-05 · Shift scheduling, visit verification and hand-offs Personas Ana (professional caregiver), Sarah (guardian), James (family, weekend shifts) Status Partially built — location check is simulated Related stories CC-38 today's schedule · CC-54 recurring shifts · CC-55 shift swap requests · CC-56 visit check-in / check-out · CC-57 late check-in alert · CC-58 structured end-of-shift hand-off · CC-59 acknowledge hand-off · CC-60 coverage gaps · CC-82 smart hand-off summary (approved addition) Last updated 2026-10-19

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
What. Sarah sets up recurring shifts and assigns caregivers, who accept them. Ana checks in at Maggie's door, which unlocks the care plan for the shift; the guardian sees who is with Maggie now. At the end of the shift Ana sends a hand-off — drafted automatically from what she logged — and the next caregiver reads and acknowledges it. Late arrivals and uncovered shifts are flagged to the guardian before they become problems.

Why. "Half my morning is figuring out what happened yesterday." (caregiver hypothesis, CC-3). Coverage problems are usually discovered too late, and verbal hand-offs lose information.

Business value. Verified visits are evidence of care for families and, later, agencies (electronic visit verification is a Release 5 item). The self-drafting hand-off removes the most-skipped paperwork from a caregiver's day.

docs.title: Check in (CC-56)
docs.text:
1. Off shift, Ana's Today with Maggie shows "Not checked in" and a locked panel: "Check in to see today's care plan."
  2. Check in opens a sheet: "Maggie's home — We check your location once, only at check-in and check-out." → Check in — I'm here (Confirming location…) → toast "Checked in — Sarah can see you're here".
  3. If location fails: Location not working? Check in manually → Why are you checking in manually? (required) → Check in manually. "Sarah will see that this check-in was manual."
Before check-in, care details are hidden (minimum necessary).

docs.title: During the shift (CC-38, CC-59)
docs.text:
1. The shift card turns teal: "On shift since 8:02 AM · 3 of 3 doses given this shift" with End shift.
  2. If the previous hand-off hasn't been read, it appears first: Last hand-off from James — mood, meals, any concern (highlighted), notes — and I've read this ("Hand-off acknowledged").
  3. A badge shows whether Maggie has checked in today. Below are Medicines and Care tasks (Medications & tasks).
On shift: the previous hand-off, then today's plan in time order.

docs.title: Smart hand-off (CC-58, CC-82)
docs.text:
1. End shift opens Hand-off. A panel Drafted from your shift contains a summary written on the device from the shift's records, for example:

    Medicines: 3 given (Lisinopril 8:00 AM, Metformin 8:00 AM, Vitamin D3 12:30 PM).
Tasks: 4 of 4 done.
Maggie checked in at 8:40 AM.

  2. Ana can edit the text or tap Redo draft. "Written on this device from what you checked off. Review and edit before sending."

  3. She picks Maggie's mood (Cheerful, Calm, Tired, Upset) and fills Meals, Anything to watch? and Notes for the next caregiver.
  4. Send hand-off and check out → "Hand-off sent — you're checked out". The Today screen shows "Thanks, Ana — your shift is complete."
  5. Alternatively Skip the hand-off → Why are you skipping? (required) → Check out without a hand-off. The activity feed records "Hand-off skipped — reason".
The draft is generated locally; nothing is sent until Ana confirms.

docs.text:
1. Ana's Your schedule shows the next two weeks (Today, then Tue, Oct 20, …) with her accepted shifts or Off.
  2. A New shift offered card appears when Sarah assigns her a shift → Accept ("Shift accepted").
  3. Swap on any day → Ask to swap this shift — choose another active family member or caregiver, add a reason → Send request ("Request sent to Sarah"). "Sarah approves the final swap."
Ana's two-week schedule.

docs.title: Guardian: schedule, late arrivals and gaps (CC-54, CC-57, CC-60)

1. Sarah's Schedule shows the next 7 days as columns with shift chips coloured by caregiver; uncovered or unaccepted shifts are striped amber (Uncovered or James (not accepted)).
  2. New shift (or tapping any chip) opens a sheet: Repeats on (day buttons), Starts, Ends, Caregiver (or Not assigned yet). "The caregiver gets a notification to accept."
  3. Coverage gaps lists uncovered shifts in the next 14 days with Assign. Visits today shows each caregiver's check-in ("In 8:02 AM · location verified" or "(manual)"), check-out and a status badge (Expected, On shift, Done).
  4. If a caregiver is more than 15 minutes late, a banner reads "Ana hasn't checked in — The 08:00 shift started 25 minutes ago." with Call.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
What. A deliberately small app for the older adult: one home screen with three large actions — What's next, SOS and Call my person — plus a morning "I'm OK" check-in, medicine reminders that can be read aloud or answered by voice, a list of decisions made about her care, and simple display settings.

Why. The landing page puts it plainly: "Designed for 81, not 21." Older adults abandon apps with menus, small text and jargon. Every elder screen shows one thing at a time, in large type, with buttons of at least 48 px.

Business value. The elder is the person whose adoption the whole circle depends on. A simple, respectful experience increases dose confirmation and daily check-ins (both inputs to the North Star) and reduces worried phone calls for the guardian.

docs.title: User journey
docs.text:
1. Maggie opens the app and sees today's date and a greeting — "Good morning, Maggie" (before noon), "Good afternoon" (until 5 PM), "Good evening".
  2. From one hour before the check-in window opens until she checks in, a banner asks "How are you this morning?" — "Let Sarah know you're OK." She taps I'm OK. Toast and spoken confirmation: "Sarah will see you're OK". The banner becomes "You checked in at 8:40 AM".
  3. The What's next tile shows the single most important item, e.g. "Up next · 6:00 PM — Metformin — 1 tablet. Take with food." A speaker button reads it aloud.
  4. She taps the tile to open the reminder card (see below) and answers I took it, Skip this time or I don't want to take it.
  5. The red SOS tile opens the hold-to-send screen (SOS & emergency).
  6. The green Call my person tile ("Sarah and 2 more") opens Who would you like to call? with large photo cards for up to three favourite people; each is a one-tap phone call.
  7. Below the tiles: Updates about me (a red dot when there is a new decision), My privacy, Emergency card and Text size.
Elder home: three actions and four small links. Reminder card with voice answer.

docs.title: Reminder card (CC-39, CC-40, CC-73)
docs.text:
1. The card shows a badge (Time to take it · time when due, Coming up · time otherwise), a drawing of the pill in its real colour and shape, name, strength and dose, instructions and "For your blood sugar. Prescribed by Dr. Hannah Brooks."
  2. I took it → "Great — marked as taken". Skip this time → "OK — marked as skipped".
  3. I don't want to take it → "That's your choice. Would you like to tell Sarah why? (optional)" with a free-text box ("For example: it upsets my stomach") → Send → "Got it. Sarah will see your note".
  4. Answer with my voice → "Listening… say "I took it" or "skip"". The answer is recorded the same way as a tap.
  5. Later today lists up to five upcoming doses and tasks.
  6. When the next item is a task (e.g. Drink a glass of water), the card shows a single Done button → "Nice work!".

docs.title: Updates about me (CC-65)
docs.text:
1. Updates about your care lists every decided request: "Sarah said yes on Mon, Oct 19. Ana asked for this.", Sarah's note, and a New badge until Maggie taps OK, got it.
  2. I have a question opens a text box → Send to Sarah. Sarah sees "Maggie has a question" at the top of Approvals.
Every decision about Maggie is visible to her.

docs.title: Make it easier to see (CC-70, CC-14, CC-48)
docs.text:
1. Text size: Large, Larger (default) or Largest text, each shown at its real size.
  2. High contrast and Read things aloud switches.
  3. Lock Circle Care: Never lock (default), After 5 minutes, After 15 minutes — "If other people use your phone, Circle Care can lock itself when you're not using it."
  4. Who we call when you press SOS shows the numbered escalation list. Want a change? Tell Sarah. sends a suggestion ("For example: call Ruth before James").
Display, lock and SOS-list settings. Call my person — up to three favourites.

An optional card on the elder home, under the three big actions. Nothing is required and there's no Submit button: every tap saves.

Change it in My privacy." while she shares, "Only you can see this." while she doesn't, and "Today stays private, because you started it while not sharing." on a private day Private days A day she starts while not sharing (or while all sharing is paused) stays private for the whole day, even if she turns sharing on later. Please tap a button." "Taken" words took, taken, take, done, yes, did "Skipped" words skip, later, not now, no (checked first) Anything else "I heard "…". Please tap a button instead." or "I didn't catch that. Please tap a button instead." Storage No audio or transcript is stored

Her choice is respected

docs.title: Accessibility
docs.text:
• Three primary targets, each the full width of the screen; all elder touch targets ≥ 48 px; settings rows ≥ 64–72 px.
  • Text sizes up to 26 px base (≈ 200% of standard), high-contrast mode, and respect for reduce motion.
  • Read-aloud uses the browser's on-device speech synthesis at a slightly slower rate (0.92).
  • Every tile has a full spoken label, e.g. "Up next · 6:00 PM: Metformin. 1 tablet. Take with food."
  • Radio groups for text size and lock use role="radio" with aria-checked.
  • Colours tuned to WCAG 2.1 AA 4.5:1 including on soft tints (CC-71); avatar initials switch between white and near-black for contrast.
  • axe-core: /app/elder, /app/elder/next, /app/elder/privacy, /app/elder/settings — 0 violations.
